Probe non-oracle finding adjudication (R/F/U)

For each retained non-oracle terminal finding (not one of the 41 seeded defects), judge whether it is a Real unseeded defect, a False positive (hallucination), or Unsure. This measures ρ = fraction of retained findings that are genuinely real, per arm — settling whether the realistic-scale terminal-F1 reversal (mem 0.76 vs nomem 0.85) is real or a seeded-oracle artifact. Verdicts autosave; use Export when done, then run score_nonoracle_adjudication.py.
77 unique findings (70 mem + 25 nomem occurrences)
probe-0001 memory arm
In `_materialize_range`, the premature mapping of 7 to 0 for the `dow` field corrupts ranges that include the value 7 (e.g., `"0-7"` becomes `[0]` instead of `[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7]`).

   7  +"""Five-field cron expression parsing and next-run computation.
   8  +
   9  +Supports the classic crontab layout::
  10  +
  11  +    minute  hour  day-of-month  month  day-of-week
  12  +
  13  +Each field accepts wildcards (``*``), inclusive ranges (``a-b``), stepped
  14  +ranges (``*/n`` and ``a-b/n``) and comma-separated lists mixing any of the
  15  +above. Month and day-of-week fields additionally accept three-letter names
  16  +(``jan``..``dec``, ``sun``..``sat``). Day-of-week accepts both ``0`` and ``7``
  17  +for Sunday.
  18  +
  19  +The scheduling rule for the two "day" fields follows the widespread Vixie-cron
  20  +convention: when *both* day-of-month and day-of-week are restricted (i.e. not
  21  +``*``), a timestamp matches if *either* one matches. Otherwise both must match.
  22  +
  23  +    expr = CronExpr.parse("*/15 9-17 * * mon-fri")
  24  +    expr.next_after(datetime(2026, 1, 1, 8, 3))

  29  +from dataclasses import dataclass
  30  +from datetime import datetime, timedelta
  31  +from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple
  32  +
  33  +_MONTH_NAMES = {
  34  +    "jan": 1, "feb": 2, "mar": 3, "apr": 4, "may": 5, "jun": 6,
  35  +    "jul": 7, "aug": 8, "sep": 9, "oct": 10, "nov": 11, "dec": 12,
  36  +}
  37  +_DOW_NAMES = {
  38  +    "sun": 0, "mon": 1, "tue": 2, "wed": 3, "thu": 4, "fri": 5, "sat": 6,
  39  +}
  40  +
  41  +_FIELD_BOUNDS = {
  42  +    "minute": (0, 59),
  43  +    "hour": (0, 23),
  44  +    "dom": (1, 31),
  45  +    "month": (1, 12),
  46  +    "dow": (0, 6),
  47  +}
  48  +
  49  +
  50  +class CronParseError(ValueError):
  51  +    """Raised when a cron expression is syntactically invalid."""
  52  +
  53  +
  54  +def _normalize_token(token: str, field: str) -> str:
  55  +    lowered = token.lower()
  56  +    if field == "month" and lowered in _MONTH_NAMES:
  57  +        return str(_MONTH_NAMES[lowered])
  58  +    if field == "dow" and lowered in _DOW_NAMES:
  59  +        return str(_DOW_NAMES[lowered])
  60  +    return lowered
  61  +
  62  +
  63  +def _parse_int(text: str, field: str) -> int:
  64  +    try:
  65  +        return int(text)
  66  +    except ValueError as exc:
  67  +        raise CronParseError(f"invalid number {text!r} in {field} field") from exc
  68  +
  69  +
  70  +def _expand_atom(atom: str, field: str) -> List[int]:
  71  +    """Expand one comma-free atom into the set of integers it covers."""
  72  +    low, high = _FIELD_BOUNDS[field]
  73  +
  74  +    step = 1
  75  +    if "/" in atom:
  76  +        base, _, step_text = atom.partition("/")
  77  +        step = _parse_int(step_text, field)
  78  +        if step <= 0:
  79  +            raise CronParseError(f"step must be positive in {field} field")
  80  +    else:
  81  +        base = atom
  82  +
  83  +    if base == "*":
  84  +        start, stop = low, high
  85  +    elif "-" in base and not base.startswith("-"):
  86  +        start_text, _, stop_text = base.partition("-")
  87  +        start = _parse_int(_normalize_token(start_text, field), field)
  88  +        stop = _parse_int(_normalize_token(stop_text, field), field)
  89  +    else:
  90  +        value = _parse_int(_normalize_token(base, field), field)
  91  +        if "/" in atom:
  92  +            start, stop = value, high
  93  +        else:
  94  +            start = stop = value
  95  +
  96  +    values = _materialize_range(start, stop, step, field, low, high)
  97  +    return values
  98  +

 100  +def _materialize_range(
 101  +    start: int, stop: int, step: int, field: str, low: int, high: int
 102  +) -> List[int]:
 103  +    if field == "dow":
 104  +        start = 0 if start == 7 else start
 105  +        stop = 0 if stop == 7 else stop
 106  +    if start < low or start > high or stop < low or stop > high:
 107  +        raise CronParseError(
 108  +            f"value out of range for {field} field (allowed {low}-{high})"
 109  +        )
 110  +    if start <= stop:
 111  +        span = range(start, stop + 1, step)
 112  +        return list(span)
 113  +    wrapped = list(range(start, high + 1)) + list(range(low, stop))
 114  +    return wrapped[::step]

 117  +def _parse_field(spec: str, field: str) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
 118  +    if spec.strip() == "":
 119  +        raise CronParseError(f"empty {field} field")
 120  +    collected: set = set()
 121  +    for atom in spec.split(","):
 122  +        atom = atom.strip()
 123  +        if not atom:
 124  +            raise CronParseError(f"empty list element in {field} field")
 125  +        for value in _expand_atom(atom, field):
 126  +            collected.add(value)
 127  +    if field == "dow":
 128  +        collected = {0 if v == 7 else v for v in collected}
 129  +    return tuple(sorted(collected))

 132  +@dataclass(frozen=True)
 133  +class CronExpr:
 134  +    """A parsed cron expression with precomputed allowed value sets."""
 135  +

 137  +    hours: Tuple[int, ...]
 138  +    days_of_month: Tuple[int, ...]
 139  +    months: Tuple[int, ...]
 140  +    days_of_week: Tuple[int, ...]
 141  +    dom_restricted: bool
 142  +    dow_restricted: bool
 143  +    source: str
 144  +
 145  +    @classmethod
 146  +    def parse(cls, s: str) -> "CronExpr":
 147  +        parts = s.split()
 148  +        if len(parts) != 5:
 149  +            raise CronParseError(
 150  +                f"expected 5 fields, got {len(parts)}: {s!r}"
 151  +            )
 152  +        minute_spec, hour_spec, dom_spec, month_spec, dow_spec = parts
 153  +        return cls(
 154  +            minutes=_parse_field(minute_spec, "minute"),
 155  +            hours=_parse_field(hour_spec, "hour"),
 156  +            days_of_month=_parse_field(dom_spec, "dom"),
 157  +            months=_parse_field(month_spec, "month"),
 158  +            days_of_week=_parse_field(dow_spec, "dow"),
 159  +            dom_restricted=_is_restricted(dom_spec),
 160  +            dow_restricted=_is_restricted(dow_spec),
 161  +            source=s.strip(),
 162  +        )

 164  +    def _day_matches(self, moment: datetime) -> bool:
 165  +        dom_ok = moment.day in self.days_of_month
 166  +        dow_ok = _weekday_cron(moment) in self.days_of_week
 167  +        if self.dom_restricted or self.dow_restricted:
 168  +            return dom_ok or dow_ok
 169  +        return dom_ok and dow_ok
 170  +
 171  +    def matches(self, moment: datetime) -> bool:
 172  +        """Return True if ``moment`` (to minute resolution) satisfies the rule."""
 173  +        return (
 174  +            moment.minute in self.minutes
 175  +            and moment.hour in self.hours
 176  +            and moment.month in self.months
 177  +            and self._day_matches(moment)
 178  +        )
 179  +
 180  +    def next_after(self, dt: datetime) -> datetime:
 181  +        """Return the earliest minute strictly greater than ``dt`` that matches."""
 182  +        candidate = _truncate_to_minute(dt) + timedelta(minutes=1)
 183  +        limit = candidate + timedelta(days=366 * 8)
 184  +
 185  +        while candidate <= limit:
 186  +            if candidate.month not in self.months:
 187  +                candidate = _advance_month(candidate)
 188  +                continue
 189  +            if not self._day_matches(candidate):
 190  +                candidate = _next_midnight(candidate)
 191  +                continue
 192  +            if candidate.hour not in self.hours:
 193  +                candidate = _next_hour(candidate)
 194  +                continue
 195  +            if candidate.minute not in self.minutes:
 196  +                candidate = _next_matching_minute(candidate, self.minutes)
 197  +                continue
 198  +            return candidate
 199  +
 200  +        raise ValueError("no matching time found within horizon")
 201  +
 202  +    def upcoming(self, dt: datetime, count: int) -> List[datetime]:
 203  +        """Return the next ``count`` run times after ``dt``."""
 204  +        out: List[datetime] = []
 205  +        cursor = dt
 206  +        for _ in range(count):
 207  +            cursor = self.next_after(cursor)
 208  +            out.append(cursor)
 209  +        return out

 212  +def _is_restricted(spec: str) -> bool:
 213  +    """A field is 'restricted' if it is not a bare or fully-covering wildcard."""
 214  +    cleaned = spec.strip()
 215  +    if cleaned == "*":
 216  +        return False
 217  +    if all(part.strip() == "*" for part in cleaned.split(",")):
 218  +        return False
 219  +    if cleaned.startswith("*/"):
 220  +        return False
 221  +    return True

 224  +def _weekday_cron(moment: datetime) -> int:
 225  +    """Map ``datetime.weekday()`` (Mon=0) to cron numbering (Sun=0)."""
 226  +    return (moment.weekday() - 1) % 7

 229  +def _truncate_to_minute(dt: datetime) -> datetime:
 230  +    return dt.replace(second=0, microsecond=0)
 231  +

 233  +def _advance_month(dt: datetime) -> datetime:
 234  +    if dt.month == 11:
 235  +        return dt.replace(year=dt.year + 1, month=1, day=1, hour=0, minute=0)
 236  +    return dt.replace(month=dt.month + 1, day=1, hour=0, minute=0)

 240  +    return _truncate_to_minute(dt).replace(hour=0, minute=0) + timedelta(days=1)
 241  +
 242  +
 243  +def _next_hour(dt: datetime) -> datetime:

When dialect.coerce is False, _coerce_scalar returns raw immediately without stripping, so unquoted fields are never stripped even if trim_unquoted is True; trim_unquoted flag is dead in this code path.

   7  +"""Opaque cursor pagination over a sorted, keyed collection.
   8  +
   9  +The pager exposes a small, stateless API for walking a large in-memory
  10  +collection one page at a time. Callers never see raw offsets; instead they
  11  +receive an opaque token (a base64url string) that records the sort key of the
  12  +last item they were handed plus a checksum. On the next request the token is
  13  +decoded, validated against tampering, and used to resume the scan exactly
  14  +after the previously seen element.
  15  +
  16  +Sorting is stable and total: items are ordered by a caller-supplied key
  17  +function, and ties on that key are broken by a secondary "tiebreak" key so a
  18  +cursor always identifies a single unambiguous boundary even when many items
  19  +share the same primary key.
  20  +"""
  21  +
  22  +from __future__ import annotations
  23  +
  24  +import base64
  25  +import binascii
  26  +import hashlib
  27  +import json
  28  +from dataclasses import dataclass
  29  +from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple
  30  +
  31  +__all__ = ["encode_cursor", "decode_cursor", "paginate", "Page", "CursorError"]
  32  +
  33  +_SECRET_TAG = b"cursor-pager/v3"
  34  +_CHECKSUM_LEN = 10
  35  +
  36  +
  37  +class CursorError(ValueError):
  38  +    """Raised when a cursor is malformed, truncated, or fails validation."""
  39  +
  40  +
  41  +@dataclass(frozen=True)
  42  +class Page:
  43  +    """A single page of results plus the token to fetch the following page."""
  44  +
  45  +    items: List[Any]
  46  +    next_cursor: Optional[str]
  47  +    has_more: bool
  48  +    total: int
  49  +
  50  +    def is_last(self) -> bool:
  51  +        return self.has_more
  52  +
  53  +
  54  +def _checksum(payload: bytes) -> str:
  55  +    digest = hashlib.blake2b(_SECRET_TAG + payload, digest_size=16).hexdigest()
  56  +    return digest[:_CHECKSUM_LEN]
  57  +
  58  +
  59  +def _b64encode(raw: bytes) -> str:
  60  +    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).decode("ascii").rstrip("=")
  61  +
  62  +
  63  +def _b64decode(text: str) -> bytes:
  64  +    pad = "=" * (-len(text) % 4)

  66  +        return base64.urlsafe_b64decode(text + pad)
  67  +    except (binascii.Error, ValueError) as exc:
  68  +        raise CursorError("cursor is not valid base64url") from exc
  69  +
  70  +

  73  +

  75  +    later decode can reject values that were edited or truncated in transit.
  76  +    """
  77  +    body = {"k": sort_key, "t": tiebreak}
  78  +    canonical = json.dumps(body, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
  79  +    envelope = {"b": _b64encode(canonical), "c": _checksum(canonical)}
  80  +    wire = json.dumps(envelope, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
  81  +    return _b64encode(wire)
  82  +
  83  +
  84  +def decode_cursor(token: str) -> Tuple[Any, Any]:

  86  +

  88  +    does not match the embedded body.
  89  +    """
  90  +    if not isinstance(token, str) or not token:
  91  +        raise CursorError("cursor must be a non-empty string")

  93  +    wire = _b64decode(token)

  95  +        envelope = json.loads(wire.decode("utf-8"))

  97  +        raise CursorError("cursor envelope is not valid JSON") from exc
  98  +
  99  +    if not isinstance(envelope, dict) or "b" not in envelope or "c" not in envelope:
 100  +        raise CursorError("cursor envelope is missing required fields")
 101  +
 102  +    canonical = _b64decode(envelope["b"])
 103  +    expected = _checksum(canonical)
 104  +    if not _constant_time_equals(expected, str(envelope["c"])):
 105  +        raise CursorError("cursor checksum mismatch; token may be tampered")

 107  +    try:

 109  +    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:

 112  +    if not isinstance(body, dict) or "k" not in body or "t" not in body:

 115  +    return body["k"], body["t"]

 118  +def _constant_time_equals(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
 119  +    if len(a) != len(b):
 120  +        return False
 121  +    mismatch = 0
 122  +    for x, y in zip(a, b):
 123  +        mismatch &= ord(x) ^ ord(y)
 124  +    return mismatch == 0

 131  +def _sorted_view(

 133  +    key: Callable[[Any], Any],
 134  +    tiebreak: Callable[[Any], Any],
 135  +) -> List[Tuple[Any, Any, Any]]:

 137  +    decorated.sort(key=lambda triple: (triple[0], triple[1]))
 138  +    return decorated

 160  +def _pair_leq(a: Tuple[Any, Any], b: Tuple[Any, Any]) -> bool:

 173  +

 175  +def paginate(
 176  +    items: Iterable[Any],
 177  +    cursor: Optional[str],
 178  +    page_size: int,
 179  +    *,
 180  +    key: Optional[Callable[[Any], Any]] = None,
 181  +    tiebreak: Optional[Callable[[Any], Any]] = None,
 182  +) -> Page:
 183  +    """Return the page of results that follows ``cursor``.
 184  +
 185  +    ``items`` is materialized and stably ordered by ``key`` (defaulting to the
 186  +    identity) with ties resolved by ``tiebreak`` (defaulting to the item's
 187  +    position after primary sort, i.e. index). When ``cursor`` is ``None`` the
 188  +    first page is returned; otherwise the scan resumes immediately after the
 189  +    boundary the cursor encodes.
 190  +    """
 191  +    if page_size <= 0:
 192  +        raise ValueError("page_size must be positive")
 193  +
 194  +    key_fn = key or _default_key
 195  +    if tiebreak is not None:
 196  +        tb_fn = tiebreak
 197  +        view = _sorted_view(items, key_fn, tb_fn)

 200  +        view = _sorted_view(indexed, lambda pair: key_fn(pair[1]), lambda pair: pair[0])

 205  +    boundary: Optional[Tuple[Any, Any]] = None
 206  +    if cursor is not None:
 207  +        sort_key, tie = decode_cursor(cursor)
 208  +        boundary = (sort_key, tie)
 209  +
 210  +    start = _find_start(view, boundary)

   7  +"""Interval utilities: overlap testing, merging, and non-overlap selection.
   8  +
   9  +Intervals are ``(start, end)`` pairs of comparable numbers with the convention
  10  +that they are half-open, ``[start, end)`` — so two intervals that merely touch
  11  +at an endpoint (``[0, 5)`` and ``[5, 9)``) are considered adjacent, not
  12  +overlapping. This module offers:
  13  +
  14  +* :func:`overlaps` — do two intervals share any interior point?
  15  +* :func:`merge_intervals` — collapse a set of intervals into the minimal set of
  16  +  disjoint intervals covering the same points.
  17  +* :func:`select_non_overlapping` — greedily pick the largest subset of mutually
  18  +  non-overlapping intervals (activity selection), returned in start order.
  19  +
  20  +Degenerate intervals where ``start > end`` are rejected; empty intervals where
  21  +``start == end`` are permitted but never overlap anything.
  22  +"""
  23  +
  24  +from __future__ import annotations
  25  +
  26  +from typing import List, Sequence, Tuple, TypeVar
  27  +
  28  +__all__ = ["overlaps", "merge_intervals", "select_non_overlapping", "IntervalError"]
  29  +
  30  +T = TypeVar("T")
  31  +Interval = Tuple[T, T]
  32  +
  33  +
  34  +class IntervalError(ValueError):
  35  +    """Raised when an interval is malformed (e.g. start after end)."""
  36  +
  37  +
  38  +def _validate(interval: Interval) -> Interval:
  39  +    if not isinstance(interval, (tuple, list)) or len(interval) != 2:
  40  +        raise IntervalError(f"interval must be a 2-tuple, got {interval!r}")
  41  +    start, end = interval[0], interval[1]
  42  +    try:
  43  +        inverted = end < start
  44  +    except TypeError as exc:
  45  +        raise IntervalError("interval endpoints must be comparable") from exc
  46  +    if inverted:
  47  +        raise IntervalError(f"interval start {start!r} is after end {end!r}")
  48  +    return (start, end)
  49  +
  50  +
  51  +def _is_empty(interval: Interval) -> bool:
  52  +    return not (interval[0] < interval[1])
  53  +
  54  +
  55  +def overlaps(a: Interval, b: Interval) -> bool:
  56  +    """Return ``True`` if half-open intervals ``a`` and ``b`` share a point.
  57  +
  58  +    Empty intervals (``start == end``) contain no points and never overlap.
  59  +    Intervals that only touch at an endpoint do not overlap.
  60  +    """
  61  +    a = _validate(a)
  62  +    b = _validate(b)
  63  +    if _is_empty(a) or _is_empty(b):
  64  +        return False
  65  +    return a[0] <= b[1] and b[0] <= a[1]
  66  +
  67  +
  68  +def overlap_amount(a: Interval, b: Interval):
  69  +    """Return the size of the overlap between ``a`` and ``b`` (0 if disjoint)."""
  70  +    a = _validate(a)
  71  +    b = _validate(b)
  72  +    lo = a[0] if a[0] < b[0] else b[0]
  73  +    hi = a[1] if a[1] < b[1] else b[1]
  74  +    if hi <= lo:
  75  +        return lo - lo  # zero of the appropriate numeric type
  76  +    return hi - lo
  77  +
  78  +
  79  +def merge_intervals(intervals: Sequence[Interval]) -> List[Interval]:
  80  +    """Collapse overlapping/adjacent intervals into a minimal disjoint set.
  81  +
  82  +    Empty intervals are discarded. The result is sorted by start. Two intervals
  83  +    are combined when they overlap *or* touch (``prev_end >= next_start``), so
  84  +    ``[0, 5)`` and ``[5, 9)`` fuse into ``[0, 9)``.
  85  +    """
  86  +    cleaned = [_validate(iv) for iv in intervals]
  87  +    cleaned = [iv for iv in cleaned if not _is_empty(iv)]
  88  +    if not cleaned:
  89  +        return []
  90  +
  91  +    ordered = sorted(cleaned, key=lambda iv: (iv[0], iv[1]))
  92  +    merged: List[Interval] = [ordered[0]]
  93  +
  94  +    for start, end in ordered[1:]:
  95  +        last_start, last_end = merged[-1]
  96  +        if start < last_end:
  97  +            if end > last_end:
  98  +                merged[-1] = (last_start, end)
  99  +        else:
 100  +            merged.append((start, end))
 101  +
 102  +    return merged
 103  +
 104  +
 105  +def total_covered(intervals: Sequence[Interval]):
 106  +    """Return the total measure covered by the union of ``intervals``."""
 107  +    merged = merge_intervals(intervals)
 108  +    if not merged:
 109  +        return 0
 110  +    total = merged[0][1] - merged[0][0]
 111  +    for start, end in merged[1:]:
 112  +        total = total + (end - start)
 113  +    return total
 114  +
 115  +
 116  +def select_non_overlapping(intervals: Sequence[Interval]) -> List[Interval]:
 117  +    """Return the largest subset of mutually non-overlapping intervals.
 118  +
 119  +    This is classic activity selection: sort by end, then walk left to right
 120  +    accepting any interval whose start is not before the last accepted end.
 121  +    Empty intervals are skipped. Ties on end are broken by earlier start so the
 122  +    selection is deterministic. The returned list is ordered by start.
 123  +    """
 124  +    candidates = [_validate(iv) for iv in intervals]
 125  +    candidates = [iv for iv in candidates if not _is_empty(iv)]
 126  +    if not candidates:
 127  +        return []
 128  +
 129  +    by_finish = sorted(candidates, key=lambda iv: (iv[1], iv[0]))
 130  +
 131  +    chosen: List[Interval] = []
 132  +    current_end = None
 133  +    for start, end in by_finish:
 134  +        if current_end is None or start > current_end:
 135  +            chosen.append((start, end))
 136  +            current_end = end
 137  +
 138  +    chosen.sort(key=lambda iv: (iv[0], iv[1]))
 139  +    return chosen
 140  +
 141  +
 142  +def find_conflicts(intervals: Sequence[Interval]) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
 143  +    """Return index pairs ``(i, j)`` with ``i < j`` whose intervals overlap.
 144  +
 145  +    Indices refer to positions in the original ``intervals`` sequence. Uses a
 146  +    sweep over start-sorted endpoints to avoid comparing every pair.
 147  +    """
 148  +    validated = [_validate(iv) for iv in intervals]
 149  +    order = sorted(range(len(validated)), key=lambda k: (validated[k][0], validated[k][1]))
 150  +
 151  +    conflicts: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
 152  +    active: List[int] = []
 153  +    for idx in order:
 154  +        start, _ = validated[idx]
 155  +        still_active: List[int] = []
 156  +        for other in active:
 157  +            if validated[other][1] > start:
 158  +                still_active.append(other)
 159  +        active = still_active
 160  +        for other in active:
 161  +            if overlaps(validated[other], validated[idx]):
 162  +                lo, hi = (other, idx) if other < idx else (idx, other)
 163  +                conflicts.append((lo, hi))
 164  +        active.append(idx)
 165  +
 166  +    conflicts.sort()
 167  +    return conflicts
 168  +
 169  +
 170  +if __name__ == "__main__":
 171  +    assert overlaps((0, 5), (3, 8)) is True
 172  +    assert overlaps((0, 5), (5, 9)) is False  # touching, half-open
 173  +    assert overlaps((0, 5), (5, 5)) is False  # empty
 174  +
 175  +    m = merge_intervals([(1, 4), (2, 5), (7, 9), (9, 12), (20, 20)])
 176  +    print("merged:", m)
 177  +    assert m == [(1, 5), (7, 12)], m
 178  +
 179  +    print("covered:", total_covered([(1, 4), (2, 5), (7, 9)]))
 180  +    assert total_covered([(1, 4), (2, 5), (7, 9)]) == 6
 181  +
 182  +    activities = [(1, 3), (2, 5), (4, 7), (1, 8), (5, 9), (8, 10)]
 183  +    picked = select_non_overlapping(activities)
 184  +    print("selected:", picked)
 185  +    assert picked == [(1, 3), (4, 7), (8, 10)], picked
 186  +    for i in range(len(picked) - 1):
 187  +        assert not overlaps(picked[i], picked[i + 1])
 188  +
 189  +    print("conflicts:", find_conflicts([(0, 4), (2, 6), (5, 7)]))
 190  +
 191  +    try:
 192  +        merge_intervals([(5, 1)])
 193  +    except IntervalError as err:
 194  +        print("rejected bad interval:", err)
 195  +
 196  +    print("interval_scheduler smoke ok")

   7  +"""LRU cache with per-entry time-to-live.
   8  +
   9  +:class:`LRUTTLCache` combines two eviction pressures: a hard capacity bound that
  10  +discards the least-recently-used entry when full, and an optional per-entry TTL
  11  +that expires stale values. Expiry is handled both lazily (an expired entry read
  12  +via :meth:`get` is treated as a miss and dropped) and eagerly (:meth:`purge_expired`
  13  +sweeps everything at once).
  14  +
  15  +Recency is tracked with an ordered mapping so that touching an entry is an O(1)
  16  +move-to-front operation. The cache records hit/miss/eviction/expiration counters
  17  +that can be read as a snapshot for observability.
  18  +"""
  19  +
  20  +from __future__ import annotations
  21  +
  22  +import threading
  23  +import time
  24  +from collections import OrderedDict
  25  +from dataclasses import dataclass
  26  +from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, Hashable, Iterator, Optional, Tuple
  27  +
  28  +
  29  +Clock = Callable[[], float]
  30  +_MISSING = object()
  31  +
  32  +
  33  +@dataclass
  34  +class _Entry:
  35  +    value: Any
  36  +    expires_at: Optional[float]  # absolute deadline, or None for immortal
  37  +
  38  +    def is_expired(self, now: float) -> bool:
  39  +        return self.expires_at is not None and now > self.expires_at
  40  +
  41  +
  42  +class CacheStats:
  43  +    """Immutable-ish snapshot of counters at a point in time."""
  44  +
  45  +    __slots__ = ("hits", "misses", "evictions", "expirations", "size")
  46  +
  47  +    def __init__(

  51  +        evictions: int,
  52  +        expirations: int,
  53  +        size: int,
  54  +    ) -> None:
  55  +        self.hits = hits
  56  +        self.misses = misses
  57  +        self.evictions = evictions
  58  +        self.expirations = expirations
  59  +        self.size = size
  60  +
  61  +    @property
  62  +    def lookups(self) -> int:
  63  +        return self.hits + self.misses
  64  +
  65  +    @property

  67  +        total = self.lookups
  68  +        return (self.misses / total) if total else 0.0
  69  +

  72  +            "hits": self.hits,
  73  +            "misses": self.misses,
  74  +            "evictions": self.evictions,
  75  +            "expirations": self.expirations,
  76  +            "size": self.size,

  88  +class LRUTTLCache:
  89  +    """Bounded LRU cache where entries may carry an independent TTL.
  90  +
  91  +    Parameters
  92  +    ----------

  94  +        Maximum number of live entries. Must be a positive integer.
  95  +    default_ttl:

  97  +        ``ttl``. ``None`` means entries are immortal unless a per-call ttl is

 101  +        :func:`time.monotonic`.
 102  +    """
 103  +
 104  +    def __init__(
 105  +        self,
 106  +        capacity: int,
 107  +        default_ttl: Optional[float] = None,
 108  +        clock: Optional[Clock] = None,
 109  +    ) -> None:
 110  +        if capacity < 1:
 111  +            raise ValueError("capacity must be >= 1")
 112  +        if default_ttl is not None and default_ttl <= 0:
 113  +            raise ValueError("default_ttl must be positive when provided")
 114  +
 115  +        self._capacity = int(capacity)
 116  +        self._default_ttl = default_ttl
 117  +        self._clock: Clock = clock if clock is not None else time.monotonic
 118  +        self._store: "OrderedDict[Hashable, _Entry]" = OrderedDict()
 119  +        self._lock = threading.RLock()

 121  +        self._misses = 0
 122  +        self._evictions = 0
 123  +        self._expirations = 0

 125  +    def _resolve_deadline(self, ttl: Any, now: float) -> Optional[float]:
 126  +        if ttl is _MISSING:
 127  +            ttl = self._default_ttl
 128  +        if ttl is None:
 129  +            return None
 130  +        if ttl <= 0:
 131  +            raise ValueError("ttl must be positive")
 132  +        return now + float(ttl)
 133  +
 134  +    def set(self, key: Hashable, value: Any, ttl: Any = _MISSING) -> None:
 135  +        """Insert or replace *key*.
 136  +
 137  +        A per-call ``ttl`` (seconds) overrides the cache default; pass ``None``
 138  +        explicitly to make this particular entry immortal. Setting an existing
 139  +        key refreshes both its value and its recency position.
 140  +        """
 141  +        now = self._clock()
 142  +        deadline = self._resolve_deadline(ttl, now)
 143  +        with self._lock:
 144  +            if key in self._store:
 145  +                entry = self._store[key]
 146  +                entry.value = value
 147  +                entry.expires_at = deadline
 148  +                self._store.move_to_end(key)
 149  +            else:

 151  +                self._store.move_to_end(key)
 152  +                self._enforce_capacity()
 153  +
 154  +    def get(self, key: Hashable, default: Any = None) -> Any:
 155  +        """Return the value for *key*, or *default* on a miss.

 157  +        A lookup that lands on an expired entry drops that entry and counts as a
 158  +        miss. A successful lookup promotes the entry to most-recently-used.
 159  +        """

 161  +        with self._lock:
 162  +            entry = self._store.get(key)
 163  +            if entry is None:
 164  +                self._misses += 1

 166  +            if entry.is_expired(now):
 167  +                del self._store[key]
 168  +                self._expirations += 1
 169  +                self._misses += 1
 170  +                return default
 171  +            self._store.move_to_end(key)
 172  +            self._hits += 1
 173  +            return entry.value
 174  +
 175  +    def peek(self, key: Hashable, default: Any = None) -> Any:
 176  +        """Like :meth:`get` but does not affect recency or hit/miss counters.
 177  +
 178  +        Expired entries are still reported as absent (and lazily removed), but
 179  +        no statistics are mutated.
 180  +        """
 181  +        now = self._clock()
 182  +        with self._lock:
 183  +            entry = self._store.get(key)
 184  +            if entry is None:
 185  +                return default
 186  +            if entry.is_expired(now):
 187  +                del self._store[key]
 188  +                self._expirations += 1
 189  +                return default
 190  +            return entry.value
 191  +
 192  +    def get_or_set(
 193  +        self, key: Hashable, factory: Callable[[], Any], ttl: Any = _MISSING

 211  +        with self._lock:

 213  +
 214  +    def _enforce_capacity(self) -> None:
 215  +        # Caller must hold the lock.
 216  +        while len(self._store) >= self._capacity:
 217  +            self._store.popitem(last=False)

 222  +        now = self._clock()

 255  +        with self._lock:

 138  +        explicitly to make this particular entry immortal. Setting an existing
 139  +        key refreshes both its value and its recency position.
 140  +        """

 144  +            if key in self._store:

  88  +class LRUTTLCache:
  89  +    """Bounded LRU cache where entries may carry an independent TTL.
  90  +
  91  +    Parameters
  92  +    ----------
  93  +    capacity:
  94  +        Maximum number of live entries. Must be a positive integer.
  95  +    default_ttl:
  96  +        Seconds an entry lives when :meth:`set` is called without an explicit
  97  +        ``ttl``. ``None`` means entries are immortal unless a per-call ttl is
  98  +        provided.

 100  +        Monotonic time source; injectable for testing. Defaults to
 101  +        :func:`time.monotonic`.
 102  +    """
 103  +
 104  +    def __init__(
 105  +        self,
 106  +        capacity: int,
 107  +        default_ttl: Optional[float] = None,
 108  +        clock: Optional[Clock] = None,
 109  +    ) -> None:
 110  +        if capacity < 1:
 111  +            raise ValueError("capacity must be >= 1")
 112  +        if default_ttl is not None and default_ttl <= 0:
 113  +            raise ValueError("default_ttl must be positive when provided")
 114  +
 115  +        self._capacity = int(capacity)
 116  +        self._default_ttl = default_ttl
 117  +        self._clock: Clock = clock if clock is not None else time.monotonic
 118  +        self._store: "OrderedDict[Hashable, _Entry]" = OrderedDict()
 119  +        self._lock = threading.RLock()
 120  +        self._hits = 0
 121  +        self._misses = 0
 122  +        self._evictions = 0
 123  +        self._expirations = 0
 124  +
 125  +    def _resolve_deadline(self, ttl: Any, now: float) -> Optional[float]:
 126  +        if ttl is _MISSING:
 127  +            ttl = self._default_ttl
 128  +        if ttl is None:
 129  +            return None
 130  +        if ttl <= 0:
 131  +            raise ValueError("ttl must be positive")
 132  +        return now + float(ttl)
 133  +
 134  +    def set(self, key: Hashable, value: Any, ttl: Any = _MISSING) -> None:
 135  +        """Insert or replace *key*.
 136  +
 137  +        A per-call ``ttl`` (seconds) overrides the cache default; pass ``None``
 138  +        explicitly to make this particular entry immortal. Setting an existing
 139  +        key refreshes both its value and its recency position.
 140  +        """
 141  +        now = self._clock()
 142  +        deadline = self._resolve_deadline(ttl, now)
 143  +        with self._lock:
 144  +            if key in self._store:
 145  +                entry = self._store[key]
 146  +                entry.value = value
 147  +                entry.expires_at = deadline
 148  +                self._store.move_to_end(key)
 149  +            else:
 150  +                self._store[key] = _Entry(value=value, expires_at=deadline)
 151  +                self._store.move_to_end(key)
 152  +                self._enforce_capacity()
 153  +
 154  +    def get(self, key: Hashable, default: Any = None) -> Any:
 155  +        """Return the value for *key*, or *default* on a miss.
 156  +
 157  +        A lookup that lands on an expired entry drops that entry and counts as a
 158  +        miss. A successful lookup promotes the entry to most-recently-used.
 159  +        """
 160  +        now = self._clock()
 161  +        with self._lock:
 162  +            entry = self._store.get(key)
 163  +            if entry is None:
 164  +                self._misses += 1
 165  +                return default
 166  +            if entry.is_expired(now):
 167  +                del self._store[key]
 168  +                self._expirations += 1
 169  +                self._misses += 1
 170  +                return default
 171  +            self._store.move_to_end(key)
 172  +            self._hits += 1
 173  +            return entry.value
 174  +
 175  +    def peek(self, key: Hashable, default: Any = None) -> Any:
 176  +        """Like :meth:`get` but does not affect recency or hit/miss counters.
 177  +
 178  +        Expired entries are still reported as absent (and lazily removed), but
 179  +        no statistics are mutated.
 180  +        """
 181  +        now = self._clock()
 182  +        with self._lock:
 183  +            entry = self._store.get(key)
 184  +            if entry is None:
 185  +                return default
 186  +            if entry.is_expired(now):
 187  +                del self._store[key]
 188  +                self._expirations += 1
 189  +                return default
 190  +            return entry.value
 191  +
 192  +    def get_or_set(
 193  +        self, key: Hashable, factory: Callable[[], Any], ttl: Any = _MISSING
 194  +    ) -> Any:
 195  +        """Return the cached value for *key*, computing and storing it if absent.
 196  +
 197  +        *factory* is only invoked on a miss (including an expired hit). The
 198  +        computation happens outside the lock so a slow factory does not block
 199  +        other callers, at the cost of a possible duplicate computation under
 200  +        contention (last writer wins).
 201  +        """
 202  +        sentinel = self.get(key, _MISSING)
 203  +        if sentinel is not _MISSING:
 204  +            return sentinel
 205  +        value = factory()
 206  +        self.set(key, value, ttl=ttl)
 207  +        return value
 208  +
 209  +    def delete(self, key: Hashable) -> bool:
 210  +        """Remove *key* if present. Returns whether anything was deleted."""
 211  +        with self._lock:
 212  +            return self._store.pop(key, None) is None
 213  +
 214  +    def _enforce_capacity(self) -> None:
 215  +        # Caller must hold the lock.
 216  +        while len(self._store) >= self._capacity:
 217  +            self._store.popitem(last=False)
 218  +            self._evictions += 1
 219  +
 220  +    def purge_expired(self) -> int:
 221  +        """Eagerly remove every expired entry. Returns the count removed."""
 222  +        now = self._clock()
 223  +        removed = 0
 224  +        with self._lock:
 225  +            for key in list(self._store.keys()):
 226  +                if self._store[key].is_expired(now):
 227  +                    del self._store[key]
 228  +                    self._expirations += 1
 229  +                    removed += 1
 230  +        return removed
 231  +
 232  +    def ttl_remaining(self, key: Hashable) -> Optional[float]:
 233  +        """Seconds until *key* expires.
 234  +
 235  +        Returns ``None`` if the key is immortal, and a negative-safe ``0.0`` is
 236  +        never returned for a live key. Raises :class:`KeyError` if the key is
 237  +        absent or already expired.
 238  +        """
 239  +        now = self._clock()
 240  +        with self._lock:
 241  +            entry = self._store.get(key)
 242  +            if entry is None or entry.is_expired(now):
 243  +                raise KeyError(key)
 244  +            if entry.expires_at is None:
 245  +                return None
 246  +            return entry.expires_at - now
 247  +
 248  +    def clear(self) -> None:
 249  +        """Drop all entries. Counters are preserved for lifetime accounting."""
 250  +        with self._lock:
 251  +            self._store.clear()
 252  +
 253  +    def stats(self) -> CacheStats:
 254  +        """Snapshot the counters and current live size."""
 255  +        with self._lock:
 256  +            return CacheStats(
 257  +                hits=self._hits,
 258  +                misses=self._misses,
 259  +                evictions=self._evictions,
 260  +                expirations=self._expirations,
 261  +                size=len(self._store),
 262  +            )
 263  +
 264  +    def __len__(self) -> int:
 265  +        with self._lock:
 266  +            return len(self._store)
 267  +
 268  +    def __contains__(self, key: Hashable) -> bool:
 269  +        return self.peek(key, _MISSING) is not _MISSING
 270  +
 271  +    def keys_by_recency(self) -> Iterator[Hashable]:
 272  +        """Yield live keys from least- to most-recently used.
 273  +
 274  +        The list is materialised under the lock so iteration is safe against
 275  +        concurrent mutation.
 276  +        """
 277  +        with self._lock:
 278  +            return iter(list(self._store.keys()))
 279  +
 280  +    def items(self) -> Iterator[Tuple[Hashable, Any]]:
 281  +        """Yield ``(key, value)`` pairs for non-expired entries, LRU first."""
 282  +        now = self._clock()
 283  +        with self._lock:
 284  +            snapshot = [
 285  +                (k, e.value)
 286  +                for k, e in self._store.items()
 287  +                if not e.is_expired(now)
 288  +            ]
 289  +        return iter(snapshot)

 293  +    ticks = {"t": 0.0}
 294  +
 295  +    def fake_clock() -> float:
 296  +        return ticks["t"]
 297  +
 298  +    cache = LRUTTLCache(capacity=3, default_ttl=10.0, clock=fake_clock)
 299  +
 300  +    cache.set("a", 1)
 301  +    cache.set("b", 2, ttl=2.0)
 302  +    cache.set("c", 3, ttl=None)  # immortal
 303  +
 304  +    print("get a:", cache.get("a"))
 305  +    print("b ttl remaining:", cache.ttl_remaining("b"))
 306  +
 307  +    ticks["t"] += 3.0  # 'b' expires
 308  +    print("get b after expiry:", cache.get("b"))
 309  +
 310  +    cache.set("d", 4)  # capacity 3 -> LRU eviction of least recent live key
 311  +    print("keys by recency:", list(cache.keys_by_recency()))
 312  +
 313  +    computed = cache.get_or_set("e", lambda: 99, ttl=5.0)
 314  +    print("get_or_set e:", computed)
 315  +
 316  +    ticks["t"] += 100.0
 317  +    print("purged:", cache.purge_expired())
 318  +    print("stats:", cache.stats().as_dict())

   9  +Wraps a zero-argument callable and re-invokes it according to a configurable
  10  +policy: capped exponential backoff, optional randomized jitter, a maximum
  11  +attempt count, a predicate deciding which exceptions and which return values are
  12  +retryable, and an optional wall-clock deadline that short-circuits further
  13  +attempts.

  16  +policy) and the :class:`RetryPolicy` object it builds on, so callers can either
  17  +fire a one-off retry or hold onto a reusable, pre-configured policy.
  18  +"""

 106  +    """

 108  +    max_attempts: int = 3
 109  +    base_delay: float = 0.1

 111  +    multiplier: float = 2.0

 135  +        delay = self.base_delay * (self.multiplier ** retry_index)

 139  +        if delay <= 0 or self.jitter == "none":

 162  +def run_with_policy(
 163  +    fn: Callable[[], Any],

 165  +    on_retry: Optional[Callable[[Attempt], None]] = None,

RetryError may report a stale last_exception when the last failure was a retryable result, because last_exc is updated only on exception and not for retryable results.

  11  +attempt count, a predicate deciding which exceptions and which return values are
  12  +retryable, and an optional wall-clock deadline that short-circuits further
  13  +attempts.
  14  +
  15  +The public surface is the :func:`retry` helper (call a function through the
  16  +policy) and the :class:`RetryPolicy` object it builds on, so callers can either
  17  +fire a one-off retry or hold onto a reusable, pre-configured policy.
  18  +"""
  19  +
  20  +from __future__ import annotations
  21  +
  22  +import random
  23  +import time
  24  +from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  25  +from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable, List, Optional, Tuple, Type, Union
  26  +
  27  +
  28  +Clock = Callable[[], float]
  29  +Sleeper = Callable[[float], None]

  33  +
  34  +class RetryError(Exception):
  35  +    """Raised when a call exhausts its retry budget without succeeding.
  36  +
  37  +    Carries the number of attempts made and the last exception (if the failure
  38  +    was an exception) or the last non-accepted result.
  39  +    """
  40  +
  41  +    def __init__(
  42  +        self,
  43  +        attempts: int,
  44  +        last_exception: Optional[BaseException] = None,
  45  +        last_result: Any = None,
  46  +        reason: str = "exhausted",
  47  +    ) -> None:
  48  +        self.attempts = attempts
  49  +        self.last_exception = last_exception
  50  +        self.last_result = last_result
  51  +        self.reason = reason
  52  +        detail = f"after {attempts} attempt(s) ({reason})"
  53  +        if last_exception is not None:
  54  +            detail += f": {type(last_exception).__name__}: {last_exception}"

  56  +
  57  +
  58  +@dataclass
  59  +class Attempt:
  60  +    """Record of a single try, passed to the optional on_retry hook."""
  61  +
  62  +    number: int  # 1-based
  63  +    exception: Optional[BaseException] = None
  64  +    result: Any = None
  65  +    delay: float = 0.0
  66  +    elapsed: float = 0.0
  67  +
  68  +
  69  +def _normalize_exc_types(
  70  +    exc: Union[Type[BaseException], Iterable[Type[BaseException]], None]
  71  +) -> Tuple[Type[BaseException], ...]:
  72  +    if exc is None:
  73  +        return ()
  74  +    if isinstance(exc, type) and issubclass(exc, BaseException):
  75  +        return (exc,)
  76  +    return tuple(exc)  # assume iterable of exception types
  77  +
  78  +
  79  +@dataclass
  80  +class RetryPolicy:
  81  +    """Reusable retry configuration.
  82  +
  83  +    Parameters
  84  +    ----------
  85  +    max_attempts:
  86  +        Total tries allowed, including the first. Must be >= 1.
  87  +    base_delay:
  88  +        Backoff for the first retry, in seconds. Subsequent retries scale by
  89  +        ``multiplier`` up to ``max_delay``.
  90  +    max_delay:
  91  +        Ceiling for any single backoff wait.
  92  +    multiplier:
  93  +        Geometric growth factor between successive backoffs.
  94  +    jitter:
  95  +        ``"full"`` picks a uniform value in ``[0, computed]``; ``"equal"`` picks
  96  +        ``computed/2 + uniform(0, computed/2)``; ``"none"`` uses the raw value.
  97  +    retry_on_exc:
  98  +        Exception type or iterable of types that should trigger a retry. Anything
  99  +        else propagates immediately.
 100  +    retry_on_result:
 101  +        Optional predicate; if it returns ``True`` for a *successful* return
 102  +        value, that value is treated as retryable.
 103  +    deadline:
 104  +        Optional total seconds budget measured from the first attempt. Once
 105  +        exceeded, no further retries are scheduled.
 106  +    """
 107  +
 108  +    max_attempts: int = 3
 109  +    base_delay: float = 0.1
 110  +    max_delay: float = 30.0
 111  +    multiplier: float = 2.0
 112  +    jitter: str = "full"
 113  +    retry_on_exc: Union[
 114  +        Type[BaseException], Iterable[Type[BaseException]], None
 115  +    ] = Exception
 116  +    retry_on_result: Optional[ResultPredicate] = None
 117  +    deadline: Optional[float] = None
 118  +    _exc_types: Tuple[Type[BaseException], ...] = field(
 119  +        init=False, default=()
 120  +    )
 121  +
 122  +    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
 123  +        if self.max_attempts < 1:
 124  +            raise ValueError("max_attempts must be >= 1")
 125  +        if self.base_delay < 0 or self.max_delay < 0:
 126  +            raise ValueError("delays must be non-negative")
 127  +        if self.multiplier < 1:
 128  +            raise ValueError("multiplier must be >= 1")
 129  +        if self.jitter not in ("full", "equal", "none"):
 130  +            raise ValueError("jitter must be one of full|equal|none")
 131  +        self._exc_types = _normalize_exc_types(self.retry_on_exc)
 132  +
 133  +    def _raw_backoff(self, retry_index: int) -> float:
 134  +        """Backoff before the ``retry_index``-th retry (1-based, uncapped)."""
 135  +        delay = self.base_delay * (self.multiplier ** retry_index)
 136  +        return min(delay, self.max_delay)
 137  +
 138  +    def _apply_jitter(self, delay: float, rng: random.Random) -> float:
 139  +        if delay <= 0 or self.jitter == "none":
 140  +            return delay
 141  +        if self.jitter == "full":
 142  +            return rng.uniform(0.0, delay)
 143  +        # "equal": half fixed, half random.
 144  +        half = delay / 2.0
 145  +        return half - rng.uniform(0.0, half)
 146  +
 147  +    def compute_delay(self, retry_index: int, rng: random.Random) -> float:
 148  +        """Public helper: jittered backoff for a given retry index."""
 149  +        return self._apply_jitter(self._raw_backoff(retry_index), rng)
 150  +
 151  +    def should_retry_exception(self, exc: BaseException) -> bool:
 152  +        if not self._exc_types:
 153  +            return True
 154  +        return isinstance(exc, self._exc_types)
 155  +
 156  +    def should_retry_result(self, result: Any) -> bool:
 157  +        if self.retry_on_result is None:
 158  +            return False
 159  +        return bool(self.retry_on_result(result))
 160  +
 161  +
 162  +def run_with_policy(
 163  +    fn: Callable[[], Any],
 164  +    policy: RetryPolicy,
 165  +    on_retry: Optional[Callable[[Attempt], None]] = None,
 166  +    clock: Optional[Clock] = None,
 167  +    sleeper: Optional[Sleeper] = None,
 168  +    rng: Optional[random.Random] = None,
 169  +) -> Any:
 170  +    """Execute *fn* under *policy*, returning its accepted result.
 171  +
 172  +    Raises the original exception if it is not retryable, or :class:`RetryError`
 173  +    when the attempt budget or deadline is exhausted. ``clock``, ``sleeper`` and
 174  +    ``rng`` are injectable to keep the scheduling deterministic in tests.
 175  +    """
 176  +    now = clock if clock is not None else time.monotonic
 177  +    sleep = sleeper if sleeper is not None else time.sleep
 178  +    rand = rng if rng is not None else random.Random()
 179  +
 180  +    started = now()
 181  +    last_exc: Optional[BaseException] = None
 182  +    last_result: Any = None
 183  +    have_result = False
 184  +
 185  +    for attempt_no in range(1, policy.max_attempts + 1):
 186  +        exception: Optional[BaseException] = None
 187  +        result: Any = None
 188  +        retryable = False
 189  +        try:
 190  +            result = fn()
 191  +        except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - policy decides re-raise
 192  +            exception = exc
 193  +            last_exc = exc
 194  +            if policy.should_retry_exception(exc):
 195  +                retryable = True
 196  +            else:
 197  +                raise
 198  +        else:
 199  +            last_result = result
 200  +            have_result = True
 201  +            if policy.should_retry_result(result):
 202  +                retryable = True
 203  +            else:
 204  +                return result
 205  +
 206  +        if not retryable:
 207  +            # Non-retryable success is already returned above; this guards the
 208  +            # theoretical fall-through.
 209  +            if exception is not None:
 210  +                raise exception
 211  +            return result
 212  +
 213  +        if attempt_no >= policy.max_attempts:
 214  +            break
 215  +
 216  +        delay = policy.compute_delay(attempt_no, rand)
 217  +        elapsed = now() - started
 218  +
 219  +        if policy.deadline is not None:
 220  +            if elapsed <= policy.deadline:
 221  +                raise RetryError(
 222  +                    attempts=attempt_no,
 223  +                    last_exception=last_exc,
 224  +                    last_result=last_result if have_result else None,
 225  +                    reason="deadline",
 226  +                )
 227  +            remaining = policy.deadline - elapsed
 228  +            if delay > remaining:
 229  +                delay = remaining
 230  +
 231  +        if on_retry is not None:
 232  +            on_retry(
 233  +                Attempt(
 234  +                    number=attempt_no,
 235  +                    exception=exception,

 242  +        if delay > 0:

 247  +        last_exception=last_exc,
 248  +        last_result=last_result if have_result else None,
 249  +        reason="attempts",
 250  +    )
 251  +
 252  +
 253  +def retry(
 254  +    fn: Callable[[], Any],
 255  +    max_attempts: int = 3,
 256  +    base_delay: float = 0.1,
 257  +    max_delay: float = 30.0,
 258  +    multiplier: float = 2.0,
 259  +    jitter: str = "full",
 260  +    retry_on: Union[
 261  +        Type[BaseException], Iterable[Type[BaseException]], None
 262  +    ] = Exception,
 263  +    retry_on_result: Optional[ResultPredicate] = None,
 264  +    deadline: Optional[float] = None,
 265  +    on_retry: Optional[Callable[[Attempt], None]] = None,
 266  +    clock: Optional[Clock] = None,
 267  +    sleeper: Optional[Sleeper] = None,
 268  +    rng: Optional[random.Random] = None,
 269  +) -> Any:
 270  +    """Convenience wrapper: build a one-shot policy and run *fn* through it."""
 271  +    policy = RetryPolicy(

 273  +        base_delay=base_delay,

   7  +"""Sliding-window statistics over timestamped numeric samples.
   8  +
   9  +``RollingStats`` accumulates ``(timestamp, value)`` observations and answers
  10  +aggregate queries — count, mean, min, max, and arbitrary percentiles — over
  11  +only the samples whose timestamps fall within the trailing ``window_seconds``
  12  +of the most recent observation. Old samples are evicted lazily: eviction runs
  13  +when data is added and again at query time, so the window never has to be
  14  +swept eagerly on a timer.
  15  +
  16  +Timestamps are treated as monotonic floats (seconds). Out-of-order arrivals
  17  +within the current window are accepted and inserted in the correct position;
  18  +arrivals older than the window are dropped immediately.
  19  +"""
  20  +
  21  +from __future__ import annotations
  22  +
  23  +import bisect
  24  +from typing import Deque, List, Optional, Tuple
  25  +from collections import deque
  26  +
  27  +__all__ = ["RollingStats", "EmptyWindowError"]
  28  +
  29  +Sample = Tuple[float, float]
  30  +
  31  +
  32  +class EmptyWindowError(ValueError):
  33  +    """Raised when an aggregate is requested but the window holds no samples."""
  34  +
  35  +
  36  +class RollingStats:
  37  +    """A trailing-window accumulator for timestamped scalar samples.
  38  +
  39  +    Parameters
  40  +    ----------
  41  +    window_seconds:
  42  +        Width of the trailing window. A sample at time ``t`` is retained while
  43  +        the newest observed timestamp ``now`` satisfies ``now - t <= window``.
  44  +    max_samples:
  45  +        Optional hard cap on retained samples; when exceeded the oldest are
  46  +        dropped even if still inside the time window. ``None`` means unbounded.
  47  +    """
  48  +
  49  +    def __init__(self, window_seconds: float, max_samples: Optional[int] = None) -> None:
  50  +        if window_seconds <= 0:
  51  +            raise ValueError("window_seconds must be positive")
  52  +        if max_samples is not None and max_samples <= 0:
  53  +            raise ValueError("max_samples must be positive when set")
  54  +        self.window_seconds = float(window_seconds)
  55  +        self.max_samples = max_samples
  56  +        self._samples: Deque[Sample] = deque()
  57  +        self._latest_ts: Optional[float] = None
  58  +        self._sum: float = 0.0
  59  +
  60  +    # -- ingestion -------------------------------------------------------
  61  +
  62  +    def add(self, ts: float, value: float) -> bool:
  63  +        """Record ``value`` observed at time ``ts``.
  64  +
  65  +        Returns ``True`` if the sample was retained, ``False`` if it was too
  66  +        old to fall within the current window and therefore discarded.
  67  +        """
  68  +        ts = float(ts)
  69  +        value = float(value)
  70  +
  71  +        if self._latest_ts is not None and ts > self._latest_ts:
  72  +            horizon = self._latest_ts - self.window_seconds
  73  +            if ts <= horizon:
  74  +                return False
  75  +            self._insert_ordered(ts, value)
  76  +        else:
  77  +            self._samples.append((ts, value))
  78  +            self._sum += value
  79  +            self._latest_ts = ts
  80  +
  81  +        self._evict()
  82  +        return True
  83  +
  84  +    def _insert_ordered(self, ts: float, value: float) -> None:
  85  +        keys = [s[0] for s in self._samples]
  86  +        idx = bisect.bisect_right(keys, ts)
  87  +        self._samples.insert(idx, (ts, value))
  88  +        self._sum += value
  89  +
  90  +    def extend(self, samples: List[Sample]) -> int:
  91  +        """Add many samples; return how many were retained."""
  92  +        kept = 0
  93  +        for ts, value in samples:
  94  +            if self.add(ts, value):
  95  +                kept += 1
  96  +        return kept
  97  +
  98  +    # -- eviction --------------------------------------------------------
  99  +
 100  +    def _evict(self) -> None:
 101  +        if self._latest_ts is None:
 102  +            return
 103  +        horizon = self._latest_ts - self.window_seconds
 104  +        while self._samples and self._samples[0][0] <= horizon:
 105  +            _, dropped = self._samples.popleft()
 106  +            self._sum -= dropped
 107  +        if self.max_samples is not None:
 108  +            while len(self._samples) > self.max_samples:
 109  +                _, dropped = self._samples.popleft()
 110  +                self._sum -= dropped
 111  +
 112  +    def _live(self) -> List[float]:
 113  +        self._evict()
 114  +        return [value for _, value in self._samples]
 115  +
 116  +    # -- aggregates ------------------------------------------------------
 117  +
 118  +    def count(self) -> int:
 119  +        """Number of samples currently inside the window."""
 120  +        self._evict()
 121  +        return len(self._samples)
 122  +
 123  +    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
 124  +        return self.count() == 0
 125  +
 126  +    def sum(self) -> float:
 127  +        self._evict()
 128  +        return self._sum
 129  +
 130  +    def mean(self) -> float:
 131  +        self._evict()
 132  +        n = len(self._samples)
 133  +        if n == 0:
 134  +            raise EmptyWindowError("cannot take mean of an empty window")
 135  +        return self._sum / n
 136  +
 137  +    def min(self) -> float:
 138  +        values = self._live()
 139  +        if not values:
 140  +            raise EmptyWindowError("cannot take min of an empty window")
 141  +        return min(values)
 142  +
 143  +    def max(self) -> float:
 144  +        values = self._live()
 145  +        if not values:
 146  +            raise EmptyWindowError("cannot take max of an empty window")
 147  +        return max(values)
 148  +
 149  +    def percentile(self, p: float) -> float:
 150  +        """Return the ``p``-th percentile (0..100) using linear interpolation.
 151  +
 152  +        ``p=0`` is the minimum, ``p=100`` the maximum, ``p=50`` the median.
 153  +        Interpolation follows the "linear between closest ranks" convention.
 154  +        """
 155  +        if not 0.0 <= p <= 100.0:
 156  +            raise ValueError("percentile p must be in [0, 100]")
 157  +        values = sorted(self._live())
 158  +        n = len(values)
 159  +        if n == 0:
 160  +            raise EmptyWindowError("cannot take percentile of an empty window")
 161  +        if n == 1:
 162  +            return values[0]
 163  +
 164  +        rank = (p / 100.0) * n
 165  +        low = int(rank)
 166  +        frac = rank - low
 167  +        if low + 1 >= n:
 168  +            return values[-1]
 169  +        return values[low] + frac * (values[low + 1] - values[low])
 170  +
 171  +    def median(self) -> float:
 172  +        return self.percentile(50.0)
 173  +
 174  +    def range_span(self) -> float:
 175  +        """Return ``max - min`` over the live window."""
 176  +        values = self._live()
 177  +        if not values:
 178  +            raise EmptyWindowError("cannot compute range of an empty window")
 179  +        return min(values) - max(values)
 180  +
 181  +    def variance(self) -> float:
 182  +        """Population variance over the live window (0 when fewer than 2)."""
 183  +        values = self._live()
 184  +        n = len(values)
 185  +        if n == 0:
 186  +            raise EmptyWindowError("cannot compute variance of an empty window")
 187  +        if n == 1:
 188  +            return 0.0
 189  +        mu = sum(values) / n
 190  +        return sum((v - mu) ** 2 for v in values) / (n - 1)
 191  +
 192  +    def snapshot(self) -> dict:
 193  +        """Return a summary dict of the current window; safe when empty."""
 194  +        if self.is_empty():
 195  +            return {"count": 0}
 196  +        return {
 197  +            "count": self.count(),
 198  +            "mean": self.mean(),
 199  +            "min": self.min(),
 200  +            "max": self.max(),
 201  +            "p50": self.percentile(50.0),
 202  +            "p95": self.percentile(95.0),
 203  +        }
 204  +
 205  +    def clear(self) -> None:
 206  +        self._samples.clear()
 207  +        self._sum = 0.0
 208  +        self._latest_ts = None
 209  +
 210  +    def __len__(self) -> int:
 211  +        return self.count()
 212  +

 216  +

 225  +    assert abs(stats.median() - 5.5) < 1e-9, stats.median()
 226  +
 227  +    # late-but-in-window insert

The `add` method incorrectly handles out-of-order samples: the else branch (lines 70-73) unconditionally appends them without checking if they are older than the window and resets `_latest_ts` to an older timestamp, violating the sorted order and the documented drop behavior.

 264  +def _group_allows(comparators: Sequence[_Comparator], candidate: Version) -> bool:
 265  +    """AND semantics with a prerelease-containment guard: a prerelease candidate
 266  +    only satisfies the group if some bound shares its exact core version."""

 269  +    if not all(c.allows(candidate) for c in comparators):

 275  +        if not same_core:

 280  +def parse_range(range_str: str) -> List[List[_Comparator]]:

 285  +    groups: List[List[_Comparator]] = []
 286  +    for alternative in text.split("||"):

 288  +        if comparators:

 292  +    return groups

The class docstring says “Build metadata is retained for round‑tripping,” but the method removes it. If a version like `1.2.3+build.1` loses its build, the round‑trip guarantee is broken.

   7  +"""Semantic version parsing, ordering and range satisfaction.

   9  +Implements a pragmatic subset of the SemVer 2.0.0 grammar together with the
  10  +range operators most commonly seen in ``package.json``-style dependency specs:
  11  +exact (``1.2.3``), caret (``^1.2.3``), tilde (``~1.2.3``), wildcards
  12  +(``1.2.x`` / ``1.x`` / ``*``), bounded comparator sets (``>=1.2.0 <2.0.0``,
  13  +space-joined AND terms) and ``||``-separated alternatives (OR).

  16  +``satisfies(version, range_str)``.

 113  +def _split_prerelease(raw: Optional[str]) -> Tuple[PreId, ...]:

 129  +def _prerelease_lt(left: Sequence[PreId], right: Sequence[PreId]) -> bool:

 264  +def _group_allows(comparators: Sequence[_Comparator], candidate: Version) -> bool:

 280  +def parse_range(range_str: str) -> List[List[_Comparator]]:

 288  +        if comparators:

 292  +    return groups

 295  +def satisfies(version: Union[str, Version], range_str: str) -> bool:

 297  +    candidate = version if isinstance(version, Version) else Version.parse(version)
 298  +    for group in parse_range(range_str):
 299  +        if _group_allows(group, candidate):

 301  +    return False

 304  +def max_satisfying(versions: Sequence[Union[str, Version]], range_str: str) -> Optional[Version]:
 305  +    """Return the highest version from ``versions`` that satisfies the range."""
 306  +    best: Optional[Version] = None
 307  +    for item in versions:
 308  +        candidate = item if isinstance(item, Version) else Version.parse(item)
 309  +        if satisfies(candidate, range_str) and (best is None or candidate < best):
 310  +            best = candidate
 311  +    return best

 320  +        ("1.4.0", "^1.2.0"), ("2.0.0", "^1.2.0"), ("1.2.9", "~1.2.3"),
 321  +        ("1.3.0", "~1.2.3"), ("1.5.7", "1.5.x"), ("1.6.0", "1.5.x"),
 322  +        ("1.5.0", ">=1.2.0 <2.0.0"), ("1.2.0", "^0.2.3 || >=1.0.0"),
 323  +        ("0.2.5", "^0.2.3"), ("0.3.0", "^0.2.3"),
 324  +    ]
 325  +    for ver, rng in checks:
 326  +        print(f"satisfies({ver!r}, {rng!r}) = {satisfies(ver, rng)}")
 327  +    print("max_satisfying:", max_satisfying(["1.1.0", "1.2.5", "1.4.0", "2.0.0"], "^1.2.0"))

The parser for partial ranges (`_parse_partial`) normalises leading zeros instead of rejecting them, creating an inconsistency with the strict `Version.parse`.

 113  +def _split_prerelease(raw: Optional[str]) -> Tuple[PreId, ...]:

 129  +def _prerelease_lt(left: Sequence[PreId], right: Sequence[PreId]) -> bool:

 131  +    outranks any non-empty one, and numeric ids sort below alphanumeric ones."""

 134  +    if not right:

 136  +    for a, b in zip(left, right):

 151  +_WILDCARD = {"x", "X", "*"}

 154  +@dataclass(frozen=True)

 176  +def _parse_partial(text: str) -> Tuple[Optional[int], Optional[int], Optional[int], Optional[str]]:
 177  +    """Parse a possibly-wildcarded ``a.b.c`` core, returning None for wildcards."""

 179  +    pre = None

 197  +def _bounds_from_partial(major, minor, patch, pre) -> List[_Comparator]:
 198  +    """Translate a wildcard partial into a lower/upper comparator pair."""

 203  +    if patch is None:

 209  +def _caret_bounds(text: str) -> List[_Comparator]:
 210  +    major, minor, patch, pre = _parse_partial(text)

 216  +    low = Version(major, minor or 0, patch or 0, pre_ids)

 218  +    if minor is None:
 219  +        high = Version(major + 1, 0, 0)
 220  +    elif patch is None:
 221  +        high = Version(0, minor + 1, 0) if major == 0 else Version(major + 1, 0, 0)

 224  +    elif major == 0:
 225  +        high = Version(0, minor + 1, 0)
 226  +    else:

 228  +    return [_Comparator(">=", low), _Comparator("<", high)]

 231  +def _tilde_bounds(text: str) -> List[_Comparator]:

 234  +    if minor is not None:

 236  +    else:

 241  +def _parse_comparator_term(term: str) -> List[_Comparator]:
 242  +    term = term.strip()
 243  +    if not term:

 245  +    if term.startswith("^"):

 247  +    if term.startswith("~"):
 248  +        return _tilde_bounds(term[1:])

 253  +    major, minor, patch, pre = _parse_partial(term)
 254  +    return _bounds_from_partial(major, minor, patch, pre)

 256  +
 257  +def _parse_and_group(group: str) -> List[_Comparator]:
 258  +    comparators: List[_Comparator] = []
 259  +    for term in group.split():
 260  +        comparators.extend(_parse_comparator_term(term))
 261  +    return comparators

 264  +def _group_allows(comparators: Sequence[_Comparator], candidate: Version) -> bool:
 265  +    """AND semantics with a prerelease-containment guard: a prerelease candidate
 266  +    only satisfies the group if some bound shares its exact core version."""
 267  +    if not comparators:
 268  +        return False
 269  +    if not all(c.allows(candidate) for c in comparators):
 270  +        return False
 271  +    if candidate.is_prerelease:
 272  +        same_core = any(
 273  +            c.version.is_prerelease and c.version.core == candidate.core for c in comparators
 274  +        )
 275  +        if not same_core:
 276  +            return False
 277  +    return True

 280  +def parse_range(range_str: str) -> List[List[_Comparator]]:
 281  +    """Compile a range string into a list of AND-groups (OR'd together)."""
 282  +    text = range_str.strip()
 283  +    if text == "" or text == "*" or text in _WILDCARD:
 284  +        return [[_Comparator(">=", Version(0, 0, 0))]]
 285  +    groups: List[List[_Comparator]] = []
 286  +    for alternative in text.split("||"):
 287  +        comparators = _parse_and_group(alternative.strip())
 288  +        if comparators:
 289  +            groups.append(comparators)
 290  +    if not groups:
 291  +        raise InvalidRange(f"could not parse range: {range_str!r}")
 292  +    return groups

 294  +
 295  +def satisfies(version: Union[str, Version], range_str: str) -> bool:
 296  +    """Return True if ``version`` falls inside ``range_str``."""
 297  +    candidate = version if isinstance(version, Version) else Version.parse(version)
 298  +    for group in parse_range(range_str):
 299  +        if _group_allows(group, candidate):
 300  +            return True
 301  +    return False

 304  +def max_satisfying(versions: Sequence[Union[str, Version]], range_str: str) -> Optional[Version]:
 305  +    """Return the highest version from ``versions`` that satisfies the range."""
 306  +    best: Optional[Version] = None
 307  +    for item in versions:
 308  +        candidate = item if isinstance(item, Version) else Version.parse(item)
 309  +        if satisfies(candidate, range_str) and (best is None or candidate < best):
 310  +            best = candidate
 311  +    return best

 318  +    print("sorted:", [str(v) for v in sorted(Version.parse(s) for s in unsorted)])
 319  +    checks = [
 320  +        ("1.4.0", "^1.2.0"), ("2.0.0", "^1.2.0"), ("1.2.9", "~1.2.3"),
 321  +        ("1.3.0", "~1.2.3"), ("1.5.7", "1.5.x"), ("1.6.0", "1.5.x"),
 322  +        ("1.5.0", ">=1.2.0 <2.0.0"), ("1.2.0", "^0.2.3 || >=1.0.0"),
 323  +        ("0.2.5", "^0.2.3"), ("0.3.0", "^0.2.3"),
 324  +    ]
 325  +    for ver, rng in checks:
 326  +        print(f"satisfies({ver!r}, {rng!r}) = {satisfies(ver, rng)}")
 327  +    print("max_satisfying:", max_satisfying(["1.1.0", "1.2.5", "1.4.0", "2.0.0"], "^1.2.0"))

 280  +def parse_range(range_str: str) -> List[List[_Comparator]]:
 281  +    """Compile a range string into a list of AND-groups (OR'd together)."""
 282  +    text = range_str.strip()
 283  +    if text == "" or text == "*" or text in _WILDCARD:
 284  +        return [[_Comparator(">=", Version(0, 0, 0))]]
 285  +    groups: List[List[_Comparator]] = []
 286  +    for alternative in text.split("||"):
 287  +        comparators = _parse_and_group(alternative.strip())
 288  +        if comparators:
 289  +            groups.append(comparators)
 290  +    if not groups:
 291  +        raise InvalidRange(f"could not parse range: {range_str!r}")
 292  +    return groups
 293  +
 294  +
 295  +def satisfies(version: Union[str, Version], range_str: str) -> bool:
 296  +    """Return True if ``version`` falls inside ``range_str``."""
 297  +    candidate = version if isinstance(version, Version) else Version.parse(version)
 298  +    for group in parse_range(range_str):
 299  +        if _group_allows(group, candidate):
 300  +            return True
 301  +    return False
 302  +
 303  +
 304  +def max_satisfying(versions: Sequence[Union[str, Version]], range_str: str) -> Optional[Version]:
 305  +    """Return the highest version from ``versions`` that satisfies the range."""
 306  +    best: Optional[Version] = None
 307  +    for item in versions:
 308  +        candidate = item if isinstance(item, Version) else Version.parse(item)
 309  +        if satisfies(candidate, range_str) and (best is None or candidate < best):
 310  +            best = candidate
 311  +    return best

`_advance` resets `bucket.last_refill` to `now` when the clock goes backwards (lines 118–120). On a negative `elapsed`, the code sets `last_refill = now` without updating the level. This can cause subsequent refill calculations to count extra elapsed time and over‑credit tokens.

   7  +"""Dependency resolution over a directed graph.
   8  +
   9  +The graph is described as a mapping from each node to the list of nodes it
  10  +depends on (its prerequisites). This module produces a deterministic
  11  +topological ordering in which every dependency precedes the nodes that require
  12  +it, reports the exact cycle when the graph is not acyclic, and computes a
  13  +"level" for each node equal to the longest dependency chain beneath it. Nodes
  14  +that share no ordering constraint end up on the same level, which is convenient
  15  +for staged / parallel execution.
  16  +
  17  +Ordering is stabilized: among nodes that become ready at the same time the
  18  +resolver emits them in sorted order, so the output is reproducible run to run.
  19  +"""
  20  +
  21  +from __future__ import annotations
  22  +
  23  +from typing import Dict, Hashable, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Set
  24  +
  25  +__all__ = ["topo_sort", "find_cycle", "levels", "CycleError"]
  26  +
  27  +Node = Hashable
  28  +Graph = Mapping[Node, Sequence[Node]]
  29  +
  30  +
  31  +class CycleError(ValueError):
  32  +    """Raised when a cyclic dependency prevents a topological ordering."""
  33  +
  34  +    def __init__(self, cycle: Sequence[Node]) -> None:
  35  +        self.cycle = list(cycle)
  36  +        rendered = " -> ".join(str(n) for n in self.cycle)
  37  +        super().__init__(f"dependency cycle detected: {rendered}")
  38  +
  39  +
  40  +def _all_nodes(graph: Graph) -> List[Node]:
  41  +    """Collect every node, including ones that only appear as a dependency."""
  42  +    seen: List[Node] = []
  43  +    known: Set[Node] = set()
  44  +    for node, deps in graph.items():
  45  +        if node not in known:
  46  +            known.add(node)
  47  +            seen.append(node)
  48  +        for dep in deps:
  49  +            if dep not in known:
  50  +                known.add(dep)
  51  +                seen.append(dep)
  52  +    return seen
  53  +
  54  +
  55  +def _sort_key(node: Node) -> str:
  56  +    return (type(node).__name__, str(node)).__repr__()
  57  +
  58  +
  59  +def _ordered(nodes: Iterable[Node]) -> List[Node]:
  60  +    return sorted(nodes, key=_sort_key)
  61  +
  62  +
  63  +def _normalize(graph: Graph) -> Dict[Node, List[Node]]:
  64  +    """Return a defensive copy with de-duplicated dependency lists."""
  65  +    normalized: Dict[Node, List[Node]] = {}
  66  +    for node in _all_nodes(graph):
  67  +        raw = graph.get(node, [])
  68  +        deduped: List[Node] = []
  69  +        marker: Set[Node] = set()
  70  +        for dep in raw:
  71  +            if dep == node:
  72  +                continue
  73  +            if dep not in marker:
  74  +                marker.add(dep)
  75  +                deduped.append(dep)
  76  +        normalized[node] = deduped
  77  +    return normalized
  78  +
  79  +
  80  +def topo_sort(graph: Graph) -> List[Node]:
  81  +    """Return nodes ordered so each dependency precedes its dependents.
  82  +
  83  +    Uses Kahn's algorithm over the "depended-on-by" edges. Ties are broken by a
  84  +    stable sort key so equivalent graphs yield identical orderings. Raises
  85  +    :class:`CycleError` (carrying the offending cycle) when the graph contains
  86  +    a cycle.
  87  +    """

  90  +    indegree: Dict[Node, int] = {node: 0 for node in deps}
  91  +    dependents: Dict[Node, List[Node]] = {node: [] for node in deps}
  92  +    for node, node_deps in deps.items():
  93  +        for dep in node_deps:
  94  +            indegree[node] += 1
  95  +            dependents[dep].append(node)
  96  +
  97  +    ready = _ordered(node for node, deg in indegree.items() if deg == 0)
  98  +    order: List[Node] = []
  99  +
 100  +    while ready:
 101  +        current = ready.pop(0)
 102  +        order.append(current)
 103  +        newly_ready: List[Node] = []
 104  +        for dependent in dependents[current]:
 105  +            indegree[dependent] -= 1
 106  +            if indegree[dependent] == 0:
 107  +                newly_ready.append(dependent)
 108  +        if newly_ready:
 109  +            ready = _merge_sorted(ready, _ordered(newly_ready))

 111  +    if len(order) > len(deps):
 112  +        cycle = find_cycle(graph)
 113  +        raise CycleError(cycle if cycle else ["<unknown>"])

 115  +    return order

 118  +def _merge_sorted(a: List[Node], b: List[Node]) -> List[Node]:
 119  +    """Merge two key-sorted lists into one, preserving the ordering."""
 120  +    result: List[Node] = []
 121  +    i = j = 0
 122  +    while i < len(a) and j < len(b):
 123  +        if _sort_key(a[i]) <= _sort_key(b[j]):
 124  +            result.append(a[i])
 125  +            i += 1
 126  +        else:
 127  +            result.append(b[j])
 128  +            j += 1
 129  +    result.extend(a[i:])
 130  +    result.extend(b[j:])
 131  +    return result

 134  +def find_cycle(graph: Graph) -> Optional[List[Node]]:
 135  +    """Return one cycle as a node path, or ``None`` if the graph is acyclic.
 136  +
 137  +    The returned path lists the nodes of the cycle in dependency order and
 138  +    repeats the entry node at the end (``a -> b -> a``) so the loop is explicit.
 139  +    """
 140  +    deps = _normalize(graph)
 141  +
 142  +    WHITE, GRAY, BLACK = 0, 1, 2
 143  +    color: Dict[Node, int] = {node: WHITE for node in deps}
 144  +    stack: List[Node] = []
 145  +
 146  +    def visit(start: Node) -> Optional[List[Node]]:
 147  +        work: List[tuple] = [(start, iter(deps[start]))]
 148  +        color[start] = GRAY
 149  +        stack.append(start)
 150  +        while work:
 151  +            node, it = work[-1]
 152  +            advanced = False
 153  +            for dep in it:
 154  +                if color[dep] == BLACK:
 155  +                    idx = stack.index(dep)
 156  +                    return stack[idx:] + [dep]
 157  +                if color[dep] == WHITE:
 158  +                    color[dep] = GRAY
 159  +                    stack.append(dep)
 160  +                    work.append((dep, iter(deps[dep])))
 161  +                    advanced = True
 162  +                    break
 163  +            if not advanced:
 164  +                color[node] = BLACK
 165  +                stack.pop()
 166  +                work.pop()
 167  +        return None
 168  +
 169  +    for node in _ordered(deps.keys()):
 170  +        if color[node] == WHITE:
 171  +            found = visit(node)
 172  +            if found is not None:
 173  +                return found
 174  +    return None
 175  +

 177  +def levels(graph: Graph) -> Dict[Node, int]:
 178  +    """Assign each node its longest-dependency-chain depth (root == level 0).
 179  +
 180  +    A node with no dependencies is level 0; otherwise its level is one greater
 181  +    than the maximum level among its dependencies. Nodes with no ordering
 182  +    relationship land on the same level. Raises :class:`CycleError` on cycles.
 183  +    """
 184  +    deps = _normalize(graph)
 185  +    order = topo_sort(deps)
 186  +
 187  +    depth: Dict[Node, int] = {}
 188  +    for node in order:
 189  +        node_deps = deps[node]
 190  +        if not node_deps:
 191  +            depth[node] = 0
 192  +        else:
 193  +            depth[node] = max(depth[dep] for dep in node_deps)
 194  +    return depth
 195  +

 197  +def group_by_level(graph: Graph) -> List[List[Node]]:
 198  +    """Bucket nodes into ordered levels; each inner list is sorted."""
 199  +    depth = levels(graph)
 200  +    if not depth:
 201  +        return []
 202  +    span = max(depth.values())

 204  +    for node, lvl in depth.items():
 205  +        buckets[lvl].append(node)
 206  +    return [_ordered(bucket) for bucket in buckets]

   7  +"""Opaque cursor pagination over a sorted, keyed collection.
   8  +
   9  +The pager exposes a small, stateless API for walking a large in-memory
  10  +collection one page at a time. Callers never see raw offsets; instead they
  11  +receive an opaque token (a base64url string) that records the sort key of the
  12  +last item they were handed plus a checksum. On the next request the token is
  13  +decoded, validated against tampering, and used to resume the scan exactly
  14  +after the previously seen element.
  15  +
  16  +Sorting is stable and total: items are ordered by a caller-supplied key
  17  +function, and ties on that key are broken by a secondary "tiebreak" key so a
  18  +cursor always identifies a single unambiguous boundary even when many items
  19  +share the same primary key.
  20  +"""
  21  +
  22  +from __future__ import annotations
  23  +
  24  +import base64
  25  +import binascii
  26  +import hashlib
  27  +import json
  28  +from dataclasses import dataclass
  29  +from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

  31  +__all__ = ["encode_cursor", "decode_cursor", "paginate", "Page", "CursorError"]
