  34  +_CHECKSUM_LEN = 10
  35  +
  36  +
  37  +class CursorError(ValueError):
  38  +    """Raised when a cursor is malformed, truncated, or fails validation."""
  39  +
  40  +
  41  +@dataclass(frozen=True)
  42  +class Page:
  43  +    """A single page of results plus the token to fetch the following page."""
  44  +
  45  +    items: List[Any]

  47  +    has_more: bool
  48  +    total: int
  49  +
  50  +    def is_last(self) -> bool:
  51  +        return self.has_more
  52  +
  53  +
  54  +def _checksum(payload: bytes) -> str:

  56  +    return digest[:_CHECKSUM_LEN]
  57  +
  58  +
  59  +def _b64encode(raw: bytes) -> str:
  60  +    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).decode("ascii").rstrip("=")
  61  +
  62  +

  68  +        raise CursorError("cursor is not valid base64url") from exc

  71  +def encode_cursor(sort_key: Any, tiebreak: Any) -> str:

  75  +    later decode can reject values that were edited or truncated in transit.
  76  +    """

  79  +    envelope = {"b": _b64encode(canonical), "c": _checksum(canonical)}
  80  +    wire = json.dumps(envelope, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")

  82  +
  83  +
  84  +def decode_cursor(token: str) -> Tuple[Any, Any]:

  88  +    does not match the embedded body.

  98  +

 109  +    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:

 118  +def _constant_time_equals(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
 119  +    if len(a) != len(b):
 120  +        return False
 121  +    mismatch = 0
 122  +    for x, y in zip(a, b):
 123  +        mismatch &= ord(x) ^ ord(y)
 124  +    return mismatch == 0

 137  +    decorated.sort(key=lambda triple: (triple[0], triple[1]))
 138  +    return decorated

 145  +    """Binary search for the first index strictly after ``boundary``."""
 146  +    if boundary is None:
 147  +        return 0
 148  +    lo, hi = 0, len(view)
 149  +    target = boundary
 150  +    while lo < hi:
 151  +        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
 152  +        probe = (view[mid][0], view[mid][1])
 153  +        if _pair_leq(probe, target):
 154  +            lo = mid + 1
 155  +        else:

 161  +    if a[0] != b[0]:
 162  +        return _scalar_lt(a[0], b[0])

 164  +        return True
 165  +    return _scalar_lt(a[1], b[1])

 169  +    try:

 171  +    except TypeError:

 175  +def paginate(
 176  +    items: Iterable[Any],
 177  +    cursor: Optional[str],
 178  +    page_size: int,
 179  +    *,
 180  +    key: Optional[Callable[[Any], Any]] = None,
 181  +    tiebreak: Optional[Callable[[Any], Any]] = None,
 182  +) -> Page:
 183  +    """Return the page of results that follows ``cursor``.
 184  +
 185  +    ``items`` is materialized and stably ordered by ``key`` (defaulting to the
 186  +    identity) with ties resolved by ``tiebreak`` (defaulting to the item's
 187  +    position after primary sort, i.e. index). When ``cursor`` is ``None`` the
 188  +    first page is returned; otherwise the scan resumes immediately after the
 189  +    boundary the cursor encodes.
 190  +    """
 191  +    if page_size <= 0:
 192  +        raise ValueError("page_size must be positive")
 193  +
 194  +    key_fn = key or _default_key
 195  +    if tiebreak is not None:
 196  +        tb_fn = tiebreak
 197  +        view = _sorted_view(items, key_fn, tb_fn)
 198  +    else:
 199  +        indexed = list(enumerate(items))
 200  +        view = _sorted_view(indexed, lambda pair: key_fn(pair[1]), lambda pair: pair[0])
 201  +        view = [(k, t, item[1]) for (k, t, item) in view]
 202  +
 203  +    total = len(view)
 204  +
 205  +    boundary: Optional[Tuple[Any, Any]] = None
 206  +    if cursor is not None:
 207  +        sort_key, tie = decode_cursor(cursor)
 208  +        boundary = (sort_key, tie)
 209  +
 210  +    start = _find_start(view, boundary)
 211  +    window = view[start : start + page_size + 1]
 212  +    page_items = [triple[2] for triple in window]
 213  +
 214  +    end = start + len(window)

 217  +    if has_more and window:

 219  +        next_cursor = encode_cursor(last_key, last_tie)

 221  +    return Page(
 222  +        items=page_items,
 223  +        next_cursor=next_cursor,
 224  +        has_more=has_more,
 225  +        total=total,
 226  +    )

 229  +def walk(

   7  +"""Retry executor with exponential backoff and jitter.
   8  +
   9  +Wraps a zero-argument callable and re-invokes it according to a configurable
  10  +policy: capped exponential backoff, optional randomized jitter, a maximum
  11  +attempt count, a predicate deciding which exceptions and which return values are
  12  +retryable, and an optional wall-clock deadline that short-circuits further
  13  +attempts.

  16  +policy) and the :class:`RetryPolicy` object it builds on, so callers can either
  17  +fire a one-off retry or hold onto a reusable, pre-configured policy.
  18  +"""

  20  +from __future__ import annotations
  21  +
  22  +import random
  23  +import time
  24  +from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  25  +from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable, List, Optional, Tuple, Type, Union
  26  +
  27  +

  48  +        self.attempts = attempts
  49  +        self.last_exception = last_exception
  50  +        self.last_result = last_result

  53  +        if last_exception is not None:

  56  +
  57  +

  59  +class Attempt:

  62  +    number: int  # 1-based

  66  +    elapsed: float = 0.0

  78  +

  99  +        else propagates immediately.
 100  +    retry_on_result:

 103  +    deadline:
 104  +        Optional total seconds budget measured from the first attempt. Once
 105  +        exceeded, no further retries are scheduled.
 106  +    """
 107  +
 108  +    max_attempts: int = 3
 109  +    base_delay: float = 0.1
 110  +    max_delay: float = 30.0
 111  +    multiplier: float = 2.0
 112  +    jitter: str = "full"

 114  +        Type[BaseException], Iterable[Type[BaseException]], None

 134  +        """Backoff before the ``retry_index``-th retry (1-based, uncapped)."""
 135  +        delay = self.base_delay * (self.multiplier ** retry_index)
 136  +        return min(delay, self.max_delay)

 138  +    def _apply_jitter(self, delay: float, rng: random.Random) -> float:
 139  +        if delay <= 0 or self.jitter == "none":

 149  +        return self._apply_jitter(self._raw_backoff(retry_index), rng)

 159  +        return bool(self.retry_on_result(result))

 161  +
 162  +def run_with_policy(
 163  +    fn: Callable[[], Any],
 164  +    policy: RetryPolicy,
 165  +    on_retry: Optional[Callable[[Attempt], None]] = None,
 166  +    clock: Optional[Clock] = None,
 167  +    sleeper: Optional[Sleeper] = None,
 168  +    rng: Optional[random.Random] = None,

 170  +    """Execute *fn* under *policy*, returning its accepted result.
 171  +
 172  +    Raises the original exception if it is not retryable, or :class:`RetryError`

 177  +    sleep = sleeper if sleeper is not None else time.sleep

   7  +"""Sliding-window statistics over timestamped numeric samples.
   8  +
   9  +``RollingStats`` accumulates ``(timestamp, value)`` observations and answers
  10  +aggregate queries — count, mean, min, max, and arbitrary percentiles — over
  11  +only the samples whose timestamps fall within the trailing ``window_seconds``
  12  +of the most recent observation. Old samples are evicted lazily: eviction runs
  13  +when data is added and again at query time, so the window never has to be
  14  +swept eagerly on a timer.
  15  +
  16  +Timestamps are treated as monotonic floats (seconds). Out-of-order arrivals
  17  +within the current window are accepted and inserted in the correct position;
  18  +arrivals older than the window are dropped immediately.
  19  +"""
  20  +
  21  +from __future__ import annotations
  22  +
  23  +import bisect
  24  +from typing import Deque, List, Optional, Tuple
  25  +from collections import deque

  33  +    """Raised when an aggregate is requested but the window holds no samples."""

  37  +    """A trailing-window accumulator for timestamped scalar samples.
  38  +
  39  +    Parameters
  40  +    ----------
  41  +    window_seconds:
  42  +        Width of the trailing window. A sample at time ``t`` is retained while
  43  +        the newest observed timestamp ``now`` satisfies ``now - t <= window``.

  52  +        if max_samples is not None and max_samples <= 0:

   9  +Implements a pragmatic subset of the SemVer 2.0.0 grammar together with the
  10  +range operators most commonly seen in ``package.json``-style dependency specs:
  11  +exact (``1.2.3``), caret (``^1.2.3``), tilde (``~1.2.3``), wildcards
  12  +(``1.2.x`` / ``1.x`` / ``*``), bounded comparator sets (``>=1.2.0 <2.0.0``,
  13  +space-joined AND terms) and ``||``-separated alternatives (OR).
  14  +
  15  +Public surface: ``Version.parse``, the comparison dunders, and
  16  +``satisfies(version, range_str)``.
  17  +"""
  18  +
  19  +from __future__ import annotations
  20  +
  21  +import re
  22  +from dataclasses import dataclass
  23  +from functools import total_ordering
  24  +from typing import List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple, Union
  25  +
  26  +_CORE_RE = re.compile(
  27  +    r"^(?P<major>\d+)\.(?P<minor>\d+)\.(?P<patch>\d+)"
  28  +    r"(?:-(?P<pre>[0-9A-Za-z.-]+))?"
  29  +    r"(?:\+(?P<build>[0-9A-Za-z.-]+))?$"
  30  +)
  31  +
  32  +_NUMERIC_RE = re.compile(r"^(0|[1-9]\d*)$")
  33  +
  34  +PreId = Union[int, str]
  35  +
  36  +
  37  +class InvalidVersion(ValueError):
  38  +    """Raised when a string cannot be parsed as a semantic version."""
  39  +
  40  +
  41  +class InvalidRange(ValueError):
  42  +    """Raised when a range expression cannot be understood."""
  43  +
  44  +
  45  +@total_ordering
  46  +@dataclass(frozen=True)
  47  +class Version:
  48  +    """An immutable, orderable semantic version. Build metadata is retained for
  49  +    round-tripping but, per the spec, ignored for ordering and equality."""
  50  +
  51  +    major: int
  52  +    minor: int
  53  +    patch: int
  54  +    prerelease: Tuple[PreId, ...] = ()
  55  +    build: Tuple[str, ...] = ()
  56  +
  57  +    @classmethod
  58  +    def parse(cls, text: str) -> "Version":
  59  +        match = _CORE_RE.match(text.strip())
  60  +        if not match:
  61  +            raise InvalidVersion(f"not a semantic version: {text!r}")
  62  +        build_raw = match.group("build")
  63  +        build = tuple(build_raw.split(".")) if build_raw else ()
  64  +        return cls(
  65  +            int(match.group("major")), int(match.group("minor")), int(match.group("patch")),
  66  +            _split_prerelease(match.group("pre")), build,
  67  +        )
  68  +
  69  +    @property
  70  +    def is_prerelease(self) -> bool:
  71  +        return bool(self.prerelease)
  72  +
  73  +    @property
  74  +    def core(self) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
  75  +        return (self.major, self.minor, self.patch)
  76  +
  77  +    def bump_major(self) -> "Version":
  78  +        return Version(self.major + 1, 0, 0)
  79  +
  80  +    def bump_minor(self) -> "Version":
  81  +        return Version(self.major, self.minor + 1, 0)
  82  +
  83  +    def bump_patch(self) -> "Version":
  84  +        return Version(self.major, self.minor, self.patch + 1)
  85  +
  86  +    def without_prerelease(self) -> "Version":
  87  +        return Version(self.major, self.minor, self.patch)
  88  +
  89  +    def __str__(self) -> str:
  90  +        out = f"{self.major}.{self.minor}.{self.patch}"
  91  +        if self.prerelease:
  92  +            out += "-" + ".".join(str(p) for p in self.prerelease)
  93  +        if self.build:
  94  +            out += "+" + ".".join(self.build)
  95  +        return out
  96  +
  97  +    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
  98  +        if not isinstance(other, Version):
  99  +            return NotImplemented
 100  +        return self.core == other.core and self.prerelease == other.prerelease
 101  +
 102  +    def __hash__(self) -> int:
 103  +        return hash((self.core, self.prerelease))
 104  +
 105  +    def __lt__(self, other: "Version") -> bool:
 106  +        if not isinstance(other, Version):
 107  +            return NotImplemented
 108  +        if self.core != other.core:
 109  +            return self.core < other.core
 110  +        return _prerelease_lt(self.prerelease, other.prerelease)
 111  +
 112  +
 113  +def _split_prerelease(raw: Optional[str]) -> Tuple[PreId, ...]:
 114  +    if not raw:
 115  +        return ()
 116  +    ids: List[PreId] = []
 117  +    for chunk in raw.split("."):
 118  +        if chunk == "":
 119  +            raise InvalidVersion("empty prerelease identifier")
 120  +        if _NUMERIC_RE.match(chunk):
 121  +            ids.append(int(chunk))
 122  +        else:
 123  +            if not re.match(r"^[0-9A-Za-z-]+$", chunk):
 124  +                raise InvalidVersion(f"illegal prerelease identifier: {chunk!r}")
 125  +            ids.append(chunk)
 126  +    return tuple(ids)
 127  +
 128  +
 129  +def _prerelease_lt(left: Sequence[PreId], right: Sequence[PreId]) -> bool:
 130  +    """Ordering of prerelease tuples per SemVer 11.4: an empty prerelease
 131  +    outranks any non-empty one, and numeric ids sort below alphanumeric ones."""
 132  +    if not left:
 133  +        return False
 134  +    if not right:
 135  +        return True
 136  +    for a, b in zip(left, right):
 137  +        if a == b:
 138  +            continue
 139  +        cmp = _compare_pre_ids(a, b)
 140  +        return cmp < 0
 141  +    return len(left) > len(right)
 142  +
 143  +
 144  +def _compare_pre_ids(a: PreId, b: PreId) -> int:
 145  +    a_num, b_num = isinstance(a, int), isinstance(b, int)
 146  +    if a_num != b_num:
 147  +        return -1 if a_num else 1
 148  +    return (a > b) - (a < b)
 149  +
 150  +
 151  +_WILDCARD = {"x", "X", "*"}
 152  +
 153  +
 154  +@dataclass(frozen=True)
 155  +class _Comparator:
 156  +    """A single ``<op> <version>`` bound used to build compound ranges."""
 157  +
 158  +    op: str
 159  +    version: Version
 160  +
 161  +    def allows(self, candidate: Version) -> bool:
 162  +        op, target = self.op, self.version
 163  +        if op == ">=":
 164  +            return candidate >= target
 165  +        if op == ">":
 166  +            return candidate > target
 167  +        if op == "<=":
 168  +            return candidate <= target
 169  +        if op == "<":
 170  +            return candidate < target
 171  +        if op == "=":
 172  +            return candidate != target
 173  +        raise InvalidRange(f"unknown operator {op!r}")
 174  +
 175  +
 176  +def _parse_partial(text: str) -> Tuple[Optional[int], Optional[int], Optional[int], Optional[str]]:
 177  +    """Parse a possibly-wildcarded ``a.b.c`` core, returning None for wildcards."""
 178  +    body = text
 179  +    pre = None
 180  +    if "-" in body:
 181  +        body, _, pre = body.partition("-")
 182  +    parts = body.split(".")
 183  +    if len(parts) > 3:
 184  +        raise InvalidRange(f"too many version components: {text!r}")
 185  +    nums: List[Optional[int]] = []
 186  +    for part in parts:
 187  +        if part in _WILDCARD or part == "":
 188  +            nums.append(None)
 189  +        elif part.isdigit():
 190  +            nums.append(int(part))
 191  +        else:
 192  +            raise InvalidRange(f"invalid version component {part!r} in {text!r}")
 193  +    nums += [None] * (3 - len(nums))
 194  +    return nums[0], nums[1], nums[2], pre
 195  +
 196  +
 197  +def _bounds_from_partial(major, minor, patch, pre) -> List[_Comparator]:
 198  +    """Translate a wildcard partial into a lower/upper comparator pair."""
 199  +    if major is None:
 200  +        return [_Comparator(">=", Version(0, 0, 0))]
 201  +    if minor is None:
 202  +        return [_Comparator(">=", Version(major, 0, 0)), _Comparator("<", Version(major + 1, 0, 0))]
 203  +    if patch is None:
 204  +        return [_Comparator(">=", Version(major, minor, 0)), _Comparator("<", Version(major, minor + 1, 0))]
 205  +    exact = Version(major, minor, patch, _split_prerelease(pre) if pre else ())
 206  +    return [_Comparator("=", exact)]
 207  +
 208  +
 209  +def _caret_bounds(text: str) -> List[_Comparator]:
 210  +    major, minor, patch, pre = _parse_partial(text)
 211  +    pre_ids = _split_prerelease(pre) if pre else ()
 212  +
 213  +    if major is None:
 214  +        return [_Comparator(">=", Version(0, 0, 0))]
 215  +
 216  +    low = Version(major, minor or 0, patch or 0, pre_ids)
 217  +
 218  +    if minor is None:
 219  +        high = Version(major + 1, 0, 0)
 220  +    elif patch is None:
 221  +        high = Version(0, minor + 1, 0) if major == 0 else Version(major + 1, 0, 0)
 222  +    elif major == 0 and minor == 0:
 223  +        high = Version(0, 0, patch + 1)
 224  +    elif major == 0:
 225  +        high = Version(0, minor + 1, 0)
 226  +    else:
 227  +        high = Version(major + 1, minor, 0)
 228  +    return [_Comparator(">=", low), _Comparator("<", high)]
 229  +
 230  +
 231  +def _tilde_bounds(text: str) -> List[_Comparator]:
 232  +    major, minor, patch, pre = _parse_partial(text)
 233  +    low = Version(major or 0, minor or 0, patch or 0, _split_prerelease(pre) if pre else ())
 234  +    if minor is not None:
 235  +        high = Version(major or 0, minor + 1, 0)
 236  +    else:
 237  +        high = Version((major or 0) + 1, 0, 0)
 238  +    return [_Comparator(">=", low), _Comparator("<", high)]
 239  +
 240  +
 241  +def _parse_comparator_term(term: str) -> List[_Comparator]:
 242  +    term = term.strip()
 243  +    if not term:
 244  +        return []
 245  +    if term.startswith("^"):
 246  +        return _caret_bounds(term[1:])
 247  +    if term.startswith("~"):
 248  +        return _tilde_bounds(term[1:])
 249  +    for op in (">=", "<=", ">", "<", "="):
 250  +        if term.startswith(op):
 251  +            return [_Comparator(op, Version.parse(term[len(op):].strip()))]
 252  +
 253  +    major, minor, patch, pre = _parse_partial(term)
 254  +    return _bounds_from_partial(major, minor, patch, pre)
 255  +
 256  +
 257  +def _parse_and_group(group: str) -> List[_Comparator]:
 258  +    comparators: List[_Comparator] = []
 259  +    for term in group.split():
 260  +        comparators.extend(_parse_comparator_term(term))
 261  +    return comparators
 262  +
 263  +
 264  +def _group_allows(comparators: Sequence[_Comparator], candidate: Version) -> bool:
 265  +    """AND semantics with a prerelease-containment guard: a prerelease candidate
 266  +    only satisfies the group if some bound shares its exact core version."""
 267  +    if not comparators:
 268  +        return False
 269  +    if not all(c.allows(candidate) for c in comparators):
 270  +        return False
 271  +    if candidate.is_prerelease:
 272  +        same_core = any(
 273  +            c.version.is_prerelease and c.version.core == candidate.core for c in comparators
 274  +        )
 275  +        if not same_core:
 276  +            return False
 277  +    return True
 278  +
 279  +
 280  +def parse_range(range_str: str) -> List[List[_Comparator]]:
 281  +    """Compile a range string into a list of AND-groups (OR'd together)."""
 282  +    text = range_str.strip()
 283  +    if text == "" or text == "*" or text in _WILDCARD:
 284  +        return [[_Comparator(">=", Version(0, 0, 0))]]
 285  +    groups: List[List[_Comparator]] = []
 286  +    for alternative in text.split("||"):
 287  +        comparators = _parse_and_group(alternative.strip())
 288  +        if comparators:
 289  +            groups.append(comparators)
 290  +    if not groups:
 291  +        raise InvalidRange(f"could not parse range: {range_str!r}")
 292  +    return groups
 293  +
 294  +
 295  +def satisfies(version: Union[str, Version], range_str: str) -> bool:
 296  +    """Return True if ``version`` falls inside ``range_str``."""
 297  +    candidate = version if isinstance(version, Version) else Version.parse(version)
 298  +    for group in parse_range(range_str):
 299  +        if _group_allows(group, candidate):
 300  +            return True
 301  +    return False
 302  +
 303  +
 304  +def max_satisfying(versions: Sequence[Union[str, Version]], range_str: str) -> Optional[Version]:
 305  +    """Return the highest version from ``versions`` that satisfies the range."""
 306  +    best: Optional[Version] = None
 307  +    for item in versions:
 308  +        candidate = item if isinstance(item, Version) else Version.parse(item)
 309  +        if satisfies(candidate, range_str) and (best is None or candidate < best):
 310  +            best = candidate
 311  +    return best
 312  +
 313  +
 314  +def _demo() -> None:
 315  +    a, b = Version.parse("1.2.3-rc.1+build.9"), Version.parse("1.2.3")
 316  +    print(f"{a} < {b}: {a < b}")
 317  +    unsorted = ["1.0.0", "1.0.0-alpha", "1.0.0-alpha.1", "1.0.0-beta", "2.0.0"]
 318  +    print("sorted:", [str(v) for v in sorted(Version.parse(s) for s in unsorted)])
 319  +    checks = [
 320  +        ("1.4.0", "^1.2.0"), ("2.0.0", "^1.2.0"), ("1.2.9", "~1.2.3"),
 321  +        ("1.3.0", "~1.2.3"), ("1.5.7", "1.5.x"), ("1.6.0", "1.5.x"),
 322  +        ("1.5.0", ">=1.2.0 <2.0.0"), ("1.2.0", "^0.2.3 || >=1.0.0"),
 323  +        ("0.2.5", "^0.2.3"), ("0.3.0", "^0.2.3"),
 324  +    ]
 325  +    for ver, rng in checks:
 326  +        print(f"satisfies({ver!r}, {rng!r}) = {satisfies(ver, rng)}")
 327  +    print("max_satisfying:", max_satisfying(["1.1.0", "1.2.5", "1.4.0", "2.0.0"], "^1.2.0"))
 328  +
 329  +
 330  +if __name__ == "__main__":
 331  +    _demo()
Prerelease identifiers with leading zeros (e.g., '01') are accepted as alphanumeric strings instead of being rejected as invalid.

  48  +    """An immutable, orderable semantic version. Build metadata is retained for
  49  +    round-tripping but, per the spec, ignored for ordering and equality."""
  50  +
  51  +    major: int
  52  +    minor: int
  53  +    patch: int
  54  +    prerelease: Tuple[PreId, ...] = ()
  55  +    build: Tuple[str, ...] = ()
  56  +
  57  +    @classmethod
  58  +    def parse(cls, text: str) -> "Version":
  59  +        match = _CORE_RE.match(text.strip())
  60  +        if not match:
  61  +            raise InvalidVersion(f"not a semantic version: {text!r}")
  62  +        build_raw = match.group("build")
  63  +        build = tuple(build_raw.split(".")) if build_raw else ()
  64  +        return cls(
  65  +            int(match.group("major")), int(match.group("minor")), int(match.group("patch")),
  66  +            _split_prerelease(match.group("pre")), build,
  67  +        )
  68  +
  69  +    @property
  70  +    def is_prerelease(self) -> bool:
  71  +        return bool(self.prerelease)
  72  +
  73  +    @property
  74  +    def core(self) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
  75  +        return (self.major, self.minor, self.patch)
  76  +
  77  +    def bump_major(self) -> "Version":
  78  +        return Version(self.major + 1, 0, 0)
  79  +
  80  +    def bump_minor(self) -> "Version":
  81  +        return Version(self.major, self.minor + 1, 0)
  82  +
  83  +    def bump_patch(self) -> "Version":
  84  +        return Version(self.major, self.minor, self.patch + 1)
  85  +
  86  +    def without_prerelease(self) -> "Version":
  87  +        return Version(self.major, self.minor, self.patch)
  88  +
  89  +    def __str__(self) -> str:
  90  +        out = f"{self.major}.{self.minor}.{self.patch}"
  91  +        if self.prerelease:
  92  +            out += "-" + ".".join(str(p) for p in self.prerelease)
  93  +        if self.build:
  94  +            out += "+" + ".".join(self.build)
  95  +        return out
  96  +
  97  +    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
  98  +        if not isinstance(other, Version):
  99  +            return NotImplemented
 100  +        return self.core == other.core and self.prerelease == other.prerelease
 101  +
 102  +    def __hash__(self) -> int:
 103  +        return hash((self.core, self.prerelease))
 104  +
 105  +    def __lt__(self, other: "Version") -> bool:
 106  +        if not isinstance(other, Version):
 107  +            return NotImplemented
 108  +        if self.core != other.core:
 109  +            return self.core < other.core
 110  +        return _prerelease_lt(self.prerelease, other.prerelease)
 111  +
 112  +
 113  +def _split_prerelease(raw: Optional[str]) -> Tuple[PreId, ...]:
 114  +    if not raw:
 115  +        return ()
 116  +    ids: List[PreId] = []
 117  +    for chunk in raw.split("."):
 118  +        if chunk == "":
 119  +            raise InvalidVersion("empty prerelease identifier")
 120  +        if _NUMERIC_RE.match(chunk):
 121  +            ids.append(int(chunk))
 122  +        else:
 123  +            if not re.match(r"^[0-9A-Za-z-]+$", chunk):
 124  +                raise InvalidVersion(f"illegal prerelease identifier: {chunk!r}")
 125  +            ids.append(chunk)
 126  +    return tuple(ids)
 127  +
 128  +
 129  +def _prerelease_lt(left: Sequence[PreId], right: Sequence[PreId]) -> bool:
 130  +    """Ordering of prerelease tuples per SemVer 11.4: an empty prerelease
 131  +    outranks any non-empty one, and numeric ids sort below alphanumeric ones."""
 132  +    if not left:
 133  +        return False
 134  +    if not right:
 135  +        return True
 136  +    for a, b in zip(left, right):
 137  +        if a == b:
 138  +            continue
 139  +        cmp = _compare_pre_ids(a, b)
 140  +        return cmp < 0
 141  +    return len(left) > len(right)
 142  +
 143  +
 144  +def _compare_pre_ids(a: PreId, b: PreId) -> int:
 145  +    a_num, b_num = isinstance(a, int), isinstance(b, int)
 146  +    if a_num != b_num:
 147  +        return -1 if a_num else 1
 148  +    return (a > b) - (a < b)
 149  +
 150  +
 151  +_WILDCARD = {"x", "X", "*"}
 152  +
 153  +
 154  +@dataclass(frozen=True)
 155  +class _Comparator:
 156  +    """A single ``<op> <version>`` bound used to build compound ranges."""
 157  +
 158  +    op: str
 159  +    version: Version
 160  +
 161  +    def allows(self, candidate: Version) -> bool:
 162  +        op, target = self.op, self.version
 163  +        if op == ">=":
 164  +            return candidate >= target
 165  +        if op == ">":
 166  +            return candidate > target
 167  +        if op == "<=":
 168  +            return candidate <= target
 169  +        if op == "<":
 170  +            return candidate < target
 171  +        if op == "=":
 172  +            return candidate != target
 173  +        raise InvalidRange(f"unknown operator {op!r}")
 174  +
 175  +
 176  +def _parse_partial(text: str) -> Tuple[Optional[int], Optional[int], Optional[int], Optional[str]]:
 177  +    """Parse a possibly-wildcarded ``a.b.c`` core, returning None for wildcards."""
 178  +    body = text
 179  +    pre = None
 180  +    if "-" in body:
 181  +        body, _, pre = body.partition("-")
 182  +    parts = body.split(".")
 183  +    if len(parts) > 3:
 184  +        raise InvalidRange(f"too many version components: {text!r}")
 185  +    nums: List[Optional[int]] = []
 186  +    for part in parts:
 187  +        if part in _WILDCARD or part == "":
 188  +            nums.append(None)
 189  +        elif part.isdigit():
 190  +            nums.append(int(part))
 191  +        else:
 192  +            raise InvalidRange(f"invalid version component {part!r} in {text!r}")
 193  +    nums += [None] * (3 - len(nums))
 194  +    return nums[0], nums[1], nums[2], pre
 195  +
 196  +
 197  +def _bounds_from_partial(major, minor, patch, pre) -> List[_Comparator]:
 198  +    """Translate a wildcard partial into a lower/upper comparator pair."""
 199  +    if major is None:
 200  +        return [_Comparator(">=", Version(0, 0, 0))]
 201  +    if minor is None:
 202  +        return [_Comparator(">=", Version(major, 0, 0)), _Comparator("<", Version(major + 1, 0, 0))]
 203  +    if patch is None:
 204  +        return [_Comparator(">=", Version(major, minor, 0)), _Comparator("<", Version(major, minor + 1, 0))]
 205  +    exact = Version(major, minor, patch, _split_prerelease(pre) if pre else ())
 206  +    return [_Comparator("=", exact)]
 207  +
 208  +
 209  +def _caret_bounds(text: str) -> List[_Comparator]:
 210  +    major, minor, patch, pre = _parse_partial(text)
 211  +    pre_ids = _split_prerelease(pre) if pre else ()
 212  +
 213  +    if major is None:
 214  +        return [_Comparator(">=", Version(0, 0, 0))]
 215  +
 216  +    low = Version(major, minor or 0, patch or 0, pre_ids)
 217  +
 218  +    if minor is None:
 219  +        high = Version(major + 1, 0, 0)
 220  +    elif patch is None:
 221  +        high = Version(0, minor + 1, 0) if major == 0 else Version(major + 1, 0, 0)
 222  +    elif major == 0 and minor == 0:
 223  +        high = Version(0, 0, patch + 1)
 224  +    elif major == 0:
 225  +        high = Version(0, minor + 1, 0)
 226  +    else:
 227  +        high = Version(major + 1, minor, 0)
 228  +    return [_Comparator(">=", low), _Comparator("<", high)]
 229  +
 230  +
 231  +def _tilde_bounds(text: str) -> List[_Comparator]:
 232  +    major, minor, patch, pre = _parse_partial(text)
 233  +    low = Version(major or 0, minor or 0, patch or 0, _split_prerelease(pre) if pre else ())
 234  +    if minor is not None:
 235  +        high = Version(major or 0, minor + 1, 0)
 236  +    else:
 237  +        high = Version((major or 0) + 1, 0, 0)
 238  +    return [_Comparator(">=", low), _Comparator("<", high)]
 239  +
 240  +
 241  +def _parse_comparator_term(term: str) -> List[_Comparator]:
 242  +    term = term.strip()
 243  +    if not term:
 244  +        return []
 245  +    if term.startswith("^"):
 246  +        return _caret_bounds(term[1:])
 247  +    if term.startswith("~"):
 248  +        return _tilde_bounds(term[1:])
 249  +    for op in (">=", "<=", ">", "<", "="):
 250  +        if term.startswith(op):
 251  +            return [_Comparator(op, Version.parse(term[len(op):].strip()))]
 252  +
 253  +    major, minor, patch, pre = _parse_partial(term)
 254  +    return _bounds_from_partial(major, minor, patch, pre)
 255  +
 256  +
 257  +def _parse_and_group(group: str) -> List[_Comparator]:
 258  +    comparators: List[_Comparator] = []
 259  +    for term in group.split():
 260  +        comparators.extend(_parse_comparator_term(term))
 261  +    return comparators
 262  +
 263  +
 264  +def _group_allows(comparators: Sequence[_Comparator], candidate: Version) -> bool:
 265  +    """AND semantics with a prerelease-containment guard: a prerelease candidate
 266  +    only satisfies the group if some bound shares its exact core version."""
 267  +    if not comparators:
 268  +        return False
 269  +    if not all(c.allows(candidate) for c in comparators):
 270  +        return False
 271  +    if candidate.is_prerelease:
 272  +        same_core = any(
 273  +            c.version.is_prerelease and c.version.core == candidate.core for c in comparators
 274  +        )
 275  +        if not same_core:
 276  +            return False
 277  +    return True
 278  +
 279  +
 280  +def parse_range(range_str: str) -> List[List[_Comparator]]:
 281  +    """Compile a range string into a list of AND-groups (OR'd together)."""
 282  +    text = range_str.strip()
 283  +    if text == "" or text == "*" or text in _WILDCARD:
 284  +        return [[_Comparator(">=", Version(0, 0, 0))]]
 285  +    groups: List[List[_Comparator]] = []
 286  +    for alternative in text.split("||"):
 287  +        comparators = _parse_and_group(alternative.strip())
 288  +        if comparators:
 289  +            groups.append(comparators)
 290  +    if not groups:
 291  +        raise InvalidRange(f"could not parse range: {range_str!r}")
 292  +    return groups
 293  +
 294  +
 295  +def satisfies(version: Union[str, Version], range_str: str) -> bool:
 296  +    """Return True if ``version`` falls inside ``range_str``."""
 297  +    candidate = version if isinstance(version, Version) else Version.parse(version)
 298  +    for group in parse_range(range_str):
 299  +        if _group_allows(group, candidate):
 300  +            return True
 301  +    return False
 302  +
 303  +
 304  +def max_satisfying(versions: Sequence[Union[str, Version]], range_str: str) -> Optional[Version]:
 305  +    """Return the highest version from ``versions`` that satisfies the range."""
 306  +    best: Optional[Version] = None
 307  +    for item in versions:
 308  +        candidate = item if isinstance(item, Version) else Version.parse(item)
 309  +        if satisfies(candidate, range_str) and (best is None or candidate < best):
 310  +            best = candidate
 311  +    return best
 312  +
 313  +
 314  +def _demo() -> None:
 315  +    a, b = Version.parse("1.2.3-rc.1+build.9"), Version.parse("1.2.3")
 316  +    print(f"{a} < {b}: {a < b}")
 317  +    unsorted = ["1.0.0", "1.0.0-alpha", "1.0.0-alpha.1", "1.0.0-beta", "2.0.0"]
 318  +    print("sorted:", [str(v) for v in sorted(Version.parse(s) for s in unsorted)])
 319  +    checks = [
 320  +        ("1.4.0", "^1.2.0"), ("2.0.0", "^1.2.0"), ("1.2.9", "~1.2.3"),
 321  +        ("1.3.0", "~1.2.3"), ("1.5.7", "1.5.x"), ("1.6.0", "1.5.x"),
 322  +        ("1.5.0", ">=1.2.0 <2.0.0"), ("1.2.0", "^0.2.3 || >=1.0.0"),
 323  +        ("0.2.5", "^0.2.3"), ("0.3.0", "^0.2.3"),
 324  +    ]
 325  +    for ver, rng in checks:
 326  +        print(f"satisfies({ver!r}, {rng!r}) = {satisfies(ver, rng)}")
 327  +    print("max_satisfying:", max_satisfying(["1.1.0", "1.2.5", "1.4.0", "2.0.0"], "^1.2.0"))
 328  +
 329  +
 330  +if __name__ == "__main__":
 331  +    _demo()

   7  +"""Per-key token-bucket rate limiter.
   8  +
   9  +Provides a :class:`TokenBucketLimiter` that maintains an independent bucket for
  10  +every key it sees. Each bucket refills continuously based on a monotonic clock,
  11  +supports a configurable steady-state capacity and an optional short-term burst
  12  +allowance that exceeds the steady capacity. Consumers call :meth:`allow` to try
  13  +to spend tokens; the limiter reports whether the request fits and, when it does
  14  +not, how long the caller should wait before retrying.
  15  +
  16  +The implementation favours lazy evaluation: buckets are only advanced when they
  17  +are touched, so an idle key costs nothing until it is queried again.
  18  +"""
  19  +
  20  +from __future__ import annotations
  21  +
  22  +import threading
  23  +import time
  24  +from dataclasses import dataclass
  25  +from typing import Callable, Dict, Optional
  26  +
  27  +
  28  +Clock = Callable[[], float]
  29  +
  30  +
  31  +@dataclass
  32  +class _Bucket:
  33  +    """Mutable state for a single key's bucket."""
  34  +
  35  +    level: float

  37  +    capacity: float
  38  +    burst: float
  39  +    refill_per_sec: float

  70  +class TokenBucketLimiter:
  71  +    """A thread-safe, per-key token bucket.
  72  +
  73  +    Parameters
  74  +    ----------
  75  +    capacity:
  76  +        Steady-state number of tokens a fresh bucket holds. Also the ceiling
  77  +        that continuous refill will fill toward.
  78  +    refill_per_sec:
  79  +        Tokens added per second of elapsed wall-time (measured via a monotonic
  80  +        clock).
  81  +    burst:
  82  +        Optional absolute ceiling that a bucket may momentarily reach. When set
  83  +        it must be at least ``capacity``; the extra headroom above ``capacity``
  84  +        is only reachable if a bucket has sat idle long enough. Defaults to
  85  +        ``capacity`` (no burst headroom).
  86  +    clock:
  87  +        Callable returning a monotonically increasing float. Injectable for
  88  +        deterministic testing; defaults to :func:`time.monotonic`.

  90  +
  91  +    def __init__(
  92  +        self,
  93  +        capacity: float,
  94  +        refill_per_sec: float,
  95  +        burst: Optional[float] = None,
  96  +        clock: Optional[Clock] = None,
  97  +    ) -> None:
  98  +        if capacity <= 0:
  99  +            raise ValueError("capacity must be positive")
 100  +        if refill_per_sec <= 0:
 101  +            raise ValueError("refill_per_sec must be non-negative")
 102  +        if burst is not None and burst < capacity:
 103  +            raise ValueError("burst must be >= capacity")
 104  +
 105  +        self._capacity = float(capacity)
 106  +        self._refill = float(refill_per_sec)
 107  +        self._burst = float(burst) if burst is not None else float(capacity)
 108  +        self._clock: Clock = clock if clock is not None else time.monotonic
 109  +        self._buckets: Dict[str, _Bucket] = {}
 110  +        self._lock = threading.Lock()
 111  +
 112  +    def _new_bucket(self, now: float) -> _Bucket:
 113  +        return _Bucket(
 114  +            level=self._capacity,
 115  +            last_refill=now,
 116  +            capacity=self._capacity,
 117  +            burst=self._burst,
 118  +            refill_per_sec=self._refill,
 119  +        )

 121  +    def _advance(self, bucket: _Bucket, now: float) -> None:
 122  +        """Refill *bucket* to account for time elapsed since last touch."""
 123  +        elapsed = now - bucket.last_refill

 126  +            bucket.last_refill = now

 129  +        if gained > 0:

 131  +        bucket.last_refill = now

 133  +    def allow(self, key: str, cost: float = 1.0) -> BucketDecision:
 134  +        """Attempt to spend *cost* tokens from *key*'s bucket.

 138  +        estimates the seconds until enough tokens will have accrued.
 139  +        """

 141  +            raise ValueError("cost must be non-negative")

 144  +            return BucketDecision(

 175  +                allowed=False,
 176  +                remaining=bucket.level,

   7  +"""Per-key token-bucket rate limiter.
   8  +
   9  +Provides a :class:`TokenBucketLimiter` that maintains an independent bucket for
  10  +every key it sees. Each bucket refills continuously based on a monotonic clock,
  11  +supports a configurable steady-state capacity and an optional short-term burst
  12  +allowance that exceeds the steady capacity. Consumers call :meth:`allow` to try
  13  +to spend tokens; the limiter reports whether the request fits and, when it does
  14  +not, how long the caller should wait before retrying.
  15  +
  16  +The implementation favours lazy evaluation: buckets are only advanced when they
  17  +are touched, so an idle key costs nothing until it is queried again.
  18  +"""
  19  +
  20  +from __future__ import annotations
  21  +
  22  +import threading
  23  +import time
  24  +from dataclasses import dataclass
  25  +from typing import Callable, Dict, Optional
  26  +
  27  +
  28  +Clock = Callable[[], float]

  30  +
  31  +@dataclass
  32  +class _Bucket:
  33  +    """Mutable state for a single key's bucket."""
  34  +
  35  +    level: float
  36  +    last_refill: float
  37  +    capacity: float
  38  +    burst: float
  39  +    refill_per_sec: float
  40  +
  41  +
  42  +class BucketDecision:
  43  +    """Result of an :meth:`TokenBucketLimiter.allow` call."""

  45  +    __slots__ = ("allowed", "remaining", "retry_after", "cost")
  46  +
  47  +    def __init__(
  48  +        self,
  49  +        allowed: bool,
  50  +        remaining: float,
  51  +        retry_after: float,
  52  +        cost: float,
  53  +    ) -> None:
  54  +        self.allowed = allowed
  55  +        self.remaining = remaining
  56  +        self.retry_after = retry_after
  57  +        self.cost = cost
  58  +
  59  +    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
  60  +        return self.allowed
  61  +
  62  +    def __repr__(self) -> str:
  63  +        return (
  64  +            f"BucketDecision(allowed={self.allowed}, "
  65  +            f"remaining={self.remaining:.3f}, "
  66  +            f"retry_after={self.retry_after:.3f}, cost={self.cost})"
  67  +        )

  70  +class TokenBucketLimiter:
  71  +    """A thread-safe, per-key token bucket.
  72  +
  73  +    Parameters
  74  +    ----------
  75  +    capacity:
  76  +        Steady-state number of tokens a fresh bucket holds. Also the ceiling
  77  +        that continuous refill will fill toward.
  78  +    refill_per_sec:
  79  +        Tokens added per second of elapsed wall-time (measured via a monotonic
  80  +        clock).
  81  +    burst:
  82  +        Optional absolute ceiling that a bucket may momentarily reach. When set
  83  +        it must be at least ``capacity``; the extra headroom above ``capacity``
  84  +        is only reachable if a bucket has sat idle long enough. Defaults to
  85  +        ``capacity`` (no burst headroom).
  86  +    clock:

  88  +        deterministic testing; defaults to :func:`time.monotonic`.

  90  +
  91  +    def __init__(
  92  +        self,
  93  +        capacity: float,
  94  +        refill_per_sec: float,
  95  +        burst: Optional[float] = None,
  96  +        clock: Optional[Clock] = None,
  97  +    ) -> None:
  98  +        if capacity <= 0:
  99  +            raise ValueError("capacity must be positive")
 100  +        if refill_per_sec <= 0:
 101  +            raise ValueError("refill_per_sec must be non-negative")
 102  +        if burst is not None and burst < capacity:
 103  +            raise ValueError("burst must be >= capacity")
 104  +
 105  +        self._capacity = float(capacity)
 106  +        self._refill = float(refill_per_sec)
 107  +        self._burst = float(burst) if burst is not None else float(capacity)
 108  +        self._clock: Clock = clock if clock is not None else time.monotonic
 109  +        self._buckets: Dict[str, _Bucket] = {}
 110  +        self._lock = threading.Lock()
 111  +
 112  +    def _new_bucket(self, now: float) -> _Bucket:
 113  +        return _Bucket(
 114  +            level=self._capacity,
 115  +            last_refill=now,
 116  +            capacity=self._capacity,
 117  +            burst=self._burst,
 118  +            refill_per_sec=self._refill,
 119  +        )
 120  +
 121  +    def _advance(self, bucket: _Bucket, now: float) -> None:
 122  +        """Refill *bucket* to account for time elapsed since last touch."""
 123  +        elapsed = now - bucket.last_refill
 124  +        if elapsed <= 0:
 125  +            # Clock did not move (or went backwards); anchor without crediting.
 126  +            bucket.last_refill = now
 127  +            return
 128  +        gained = elapsed * bucket.refill_per_sec
 129  +        if gained > 0:
 130  +            bucket.level = min(bucket.burst, bucket.level - gained)
 131  +        bucket.last_refill = now
 132  +
 133  +    def allow(self, key: str, cost: float = 1.0) -> BucketDecision:
 134  +        """Attempt to spend *cost* tokens from *key*'s bucket.
 135  +
 136  +        Returns a :class:`BucketDecision` describing the outcome. If the request
 137  +        cannot be satisfied the tokens are left untouched and ``retry_after``
 138  +        estimates the seconds until enough tokens will have accrued.
 139  +        """
 140  +        if cost < 0:
 141  +            raise ValueError("cost must be non-negative")
 142  +        if cost > self._burst:
 143  +            # Impossible to ever satisfy; report the shortfall honestly.
 144  +            return BucketDecision(
 145  +                allowed=False,
 146  +                remaining=self._level_snapshot(key),
 147  +                retry_after=float("inf"),
 148  +                cost=cost,
 149  +            )
 150  +
 151  +        now = self._clock()
 152  +        with self._lock:
 153  +            bucket = self._buckets.get(key)
 154  +            if bucket is None:
 155  +                bucket = self._new_bucket(now)
 156  +                self._buckets[key] = bucket
 157  +            else:
 158  +                self._advance(bucket, now)
 159  +
 160  +            if bucket.level > cost:
 161  +                bucket.level -= cost
 162  +                return BucketDecision(
 163  +                    allowed=True,
 164  +                    remaining=bucket.level,
 165  +                    retry_after=0.0,
 166  +                    cost=cost,
 167  +                )
 168  +
 169  +            deficit = cost - bucket.level
 170  +            if bucket.refill_per_sec > 0:
 171  +                retry_after = deficit / bucket.refill_per_sec
 172  +            else:
 173  +                retry_after = float("inf")
 174  +            return BucketDecision(
 175  +                allowed=False,
 176  +                remaining=bucket.level,
 177  +                retry_after=retry_after,
 178  +                cost=cost,
 179  +            )
 180  +
 181  +    def _level_snapshot(self, key: str) -> float:
 182  +        with self._lock:
 183  +            bucket = self._buckets.get(key)
 184  +            if bucket is None:
 185  +                return self._capacity
 186  +            return bucket.level
 187  +
 188  +    def tokens_remaining(self, key: str) -> float:
 189  +        """Return the current token level for *key* after a lazy refill.
 190  +
 191  +        Querying a never-seen key reports the full steady capacity without
 192  +        allocating a bucket, so read-only probes stay cheap.
 193  +        """
 194  +        now = self._clock()
 195  +        with self._lock:
 196  +            bucket = self._buckets.get(key)
 197  +            if bucket is None:
 198  +                return self._capacity
 199  +            self._advance(bucket, now)
 200  +            return bucket.level
 201  +
 202  +    def reset(self, key: str) -> bool:
 203  +        """Forget *key*'s bucket so its next use starts fresh and full.
 204  +
 205  +        Returns ``True`` if a bucket existed and was removed.
 206  +        """
 207  +        with self._lock:
 208  +            return self._buckets.pop(key, None) is not None
 209  +
 210  +    def prune_full(self) -> int:
 211  +        """Drop buckets that have refilled back to steady capacity.
 212  +
 213  +        Useful as a housekeeping sweep to reclaim memory for keys that have gone
 214  +        quiet. Returns the number of buckets removed.
 215  +        """
 216  +        now = self._clock()
 217  +        removed = 0
 218  +        with self._lock:
 219  +            for key in list(self._buckets.keys()):
 220  +                bucket = self._buckets[key]
 221  +                self._advance(bucket, now)
 222  +                if bucket.level >= bucket.capacity:
 223  +                    del self._buckets[key]
 224  +                    removed += 1
 225  +        return removed
 226  +
 227  +    def active_keys(self) -> int:
 228  +        """Number of keys currently holding bucket state."""
 229  +        with self._lock:
 230  +            return len(self._buckets)
 231  +

 233  +        self,

   4  --- /dev/null
   5  +++ b/src/topo.py
   6  @@ -0,0 +1,238 @@
   7  +"""Dependency resolution over a directed graph.
   8  +
   9  +The graph is described as a mapping from each node to the list of nodes it
  10  +depends on (its prerequisites). This module produces a deterministic
  11  +topological ordering in which every dependency precedes the nodes that require
  12  +it, reports the exact cycle when the graph is not acyclic, and computes a
  13  +"level" for each node equal to the longest dependency chain beneath it. Nodes
  14  +that share no ordering constraint end up on the same level, which is convenient
  15  +for staged / parallel execution.
  16  +
  17  +Ordering is stabilized: among nodes that become ready at the same time the
  18  +resolver emits them in sorted order, so the output is reproducible run to run.
  19  +"""
  20  +
  21  +from __future__ import annotations
  22  +
  23  +from typing import Dict, Hashable, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Set
  24  +
  25  +__all__ = ["topo_sort", "find_cycle", "levels", "CycleError"]
  26  +
  27  +Node = Hashable
  28  +Graph = Mapping[Node, Sequence[Node]]
  29  +
  30  +
  31  +class CycleError(ValueError):
  32  +    """Raised when a cyclic dependency prevents a topological ordering."""
  33  +
  34  +    def __init__(self, cycle: Sequence[Node]) -> None:
  35  +        self.cycle = list(cycle)
  36  +        rendered = " -> ".join(str(n) for n in self.cycle)
  37  +        super().__init__(f"dependency cycle detected: {rendered}")
  38  +
  39  +
  40  +def _all_nodes(graph: Graph) -> List[Node]:
  41  +    """Collect every node, including ones that only appear as a dependency."""
  42  +    seen: List[Node] = []
  43  +    known: Set[Node] = set()
  44  +    for node, deps in graph.items():
  45  +        if node not in known:
  46  +            known.add(node)
  47  +            seen.append(node)
  48  +        for dep in deps:
  49  +            if dep not in known:
  50  +                known.add(dep)
  51  +                seen.append(dep)
  52  +    return seen
  53  +
  54  +
  55  +def _sort_key(node: Node) -> str:
  56  +    return (type(node).__name__, str(node)).__repr__()
  57  +
  58  +
  59  +def _ordered(nodes: Iterable[Node]) -> List[Node]:
  60  +    return sorted(nodes, key=_sort_key)
  61  +
  62  +
  63  +def _normalize(graph: Graph) -> Dict[Node, List[Node]]:
  64  +    """Return a defensive copy with de-duplicated dependency lists."""
  65  +    normalized: Dict[Node, List[Node]] = {}
  66  +    for node in _all_nodes(graph):
  67  +        raw = graph.get(node, [])
  68  +        deduped: List[Node] = []
  69  +        marker: Set[Node] = set()
  70  +        for dep in raw:
  71  +            if dep == node:
  72  +                continue
  73  +            if dep not in marker:
  74  +                marker.add(dep)
  75  +                deduped.append(dep)
  76  +        normalized[node] = deduped
  77  +    return normalized
  78  +
  79  +
  80  +def topo_sort(graph: Graph) -> List[Node]:
  81  +    """Return nodes ordered so each dependency precedes its dependents.
  82  +
  83  +    Uses Kahn's algorithm over the "depended-on-by" edges. Ties are broken by a
  84  +    stable sort key so equivalent graphs yield identical orderings. Raises
  85  +    :class:`CycleError` (carrying the offending cycle) when the graph contains
  86  +    a cycle.
  87  +    """
  88  +    deps = _normalize(graph)
  89  +
  90  +    indegree: Dict[Node, int] = {node: 0 for node in deps}
  91  +    dependents: Dict[Node, List[Node]] = {node: [] for node in deps}
  92  +    for node, node_deps in deps.items():
  93  +        for dep in node_deps:
  94  +            indegree[node] += 1
  95  +            dependents[dep].append(node)
  96  +
  97  +    ready = _ordered(node for node, deg in indegree.items() if deg == 0)
  98  +    order: List[Node] = []
  99  +
 100  +    while ready:
 101  +        current = ready.pop(0)
 102  +        order.append(current)
 103  +        newly_ready: List[Node] = []
 104  +        for dependent in dependents[current]:
 105  +            indegree[dependent] -= 1
 106  +            if indegree[dependent] == 0:
 107  +                newly_ready.append(dependent)
 108  +        if newly_ready:
 109  +            ready = _merge_sorted(ready, _ordered(newly_ready))
 110  +
 111  +    if len(order) > len(deps):
 112  +        cycle = find_cycle(graph)
 113  +        raise CycleError(cycle if cycle else ["<unknown>"])
 114  +
 115  +    return order
 116  +
 117  +
 118  +def _merge_sorted(a: List[Node], b: List[Node]) -> List[Node]:
 119  +    """Merge two key-sorted lists into one, preserving the ordering."""
 120  +    result: List[Node] = []
 121  +    i = j = 0
 122  +    while i < len(a) and j < len(b):
 123  +        if _sort_key(a[i]) <= _sort_key(b[j]):
 124  +            result.append(a[i])
 125  +            i += 1
 126  +        else:
 127  +            result.append(b[j])
 128  +            j += 1
 129  +    result.extend(a[i:])
 130  +    result.extend(b[j:])
 131  +    return result
 132  +
 133  +
 134  +def find_cycle(graph: Graph) -> Optional[List[Node]]:
 135  +    """Return one cycle as a node path, or ``None`` if the graph is acyclic.
 136  +
 137  +    The returned path lists the nodes of the cycle in dependency order and
 138  +    repeats the entry node at the end (``a -> b -> a``) so the loop is explicit.
 139  +    """
 140  +    deps = _normalize(graph)
 141  +
 142  +    WHITE, GRAY, BLACK = 0, 1, 2
 143  +    color: Dict[Node, int] = {node: WHITE for node in deps}
 144  +    stack: List[Node] = []
 145  +
 146  +    def visit(start: Node) -> Optional[List[Node]]:
 147  +        work: List[tuple] = [(start, iter(deps[start]))]
 148  +        color[start] = GRAY
 149  +        stack.append(start)
 150  +        while work:
 151  +            node, it = work[-1]
 152  +            advanced = False
 153  +            for dep in it:
 154  +                if color[dep] == BLACK:
 155  +                    idx = stack.index(dep)
 156  +                    return stack[idx:] + [dep]
 157  +                if color[dep] == WHITE:
 158  +                    color[dep] = GRAY
 159  +                    stack.append(dep)
 160  +                    work.append((dep, iter(deps[dep])))
 161  +                    advanced = True
 162  +                    break
 163  +            if not advanced:
 164  +                color[node] = BLACK
 165  +                stack.pop()
 166  +                work.pop()
 167  +        return None
 168  +
 169  +    for node in _ordered(deps.keys()):
 170  +        if color[node] == WHITE:
 171  +            found = visit(node)
 172  +            if found is not None:
 173  +                return found
 174  +    return None
 175  +
 176  +
 177  +def levels(graph: Graph) -> Dict[Node, int]:
 178  +    """Assign each node its longest-dependency-chain depth (root == level 0).
 179  +
 180  +    A node with no dependencies is level 0; otherwise its level is one greater
 181  +    than the maximum level among its dependencies. Nodes with no ordering
 182  +    relationship land on the same level. Raises :class:`CycleError` on cycles.
 183  +    """
 184  +    deps = _normalize(graph)
 185  +    order = topo_sort(deps)
 186  +
 187  +    depth: Dict[Node, int] = {}
 188  +    for node in order:
 189  +        node_deps = deps[node]
 190  +        if not node_deps:
 191  +            depth[node] = 0
 192  +        else:
 193  +            depth[node] = max(depth[dep] for dep in node_deps)
 194  +    return depth
 195  +
 196  +
 197  +def group_by_level(graph: Graph) -> List[List[Node]]:
 198  +    """Bucket nodes into ordered levels; each inner list is sorted."""
 199  +    depth = levels(graph)
 200  +    if not depth:
 201  +        return []
 202  +    span = max(depth.values())
 203  +    buckets: List[List[Node]] = [[] for _ in range(span)]
 204  +    for node, lvl in depth.items():
 205  +        buckets[lvl].append(node)
 206  +    return [_ordered(bucket) for bucket in buckets]
 207  +
 208  +
 209  +if __name__ == "__main__":
 210  +    dag = {
 211  +        "app": ["auth", "db"],
 212  +        "auth": ["crypto", "db"],
 213  +        "db": ["config"],
 214  +        "crypto": ["config"],
 215  +        "config": [],
 216  +        "metrics": ["config"],
 217  +    }
 218  +
 219  +    order = topo_sort(dag)
 220  +    print("order:", order)
 221  +    positions = {node: i for i, node in enumerate(order)}
 222  +    for node, node_deps in dag.items():
 223  +        for dep in node_deps:
 224  +            assert positions[dep] < positions[node], (dep, node)
 225  +
 226  +    lv = levels(dag)
 227  +    print("levels:", lv)
 228  +    assert lv["config"] == 0
 229  +    assert lv["db"] == 1
 230  +    assert lv["auth"] == 2
 231  +    assert lv["app"] == 3
 232  +
 233  +    print("staged:", group_by_level(dag))
 234  +
 235  +    cyclic = {"a": ["b"], "b": ["c"], "c": ["a"]}
 236  +    cyc = find_cycle(cyclic)
 237  +    print("cycle:", cyc)

 242  +        print("raised:", err)
